a41.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a41.name: Donald Trump
a41.title: US President
a41.speech: "We have completed our very successful attack on the three nuclear sites in Iran, including Fordow, Natanz, and Esfahan. All planes are now outside of Iran's space," ; "All planes are safely on their way home,"

a41.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a41.name: Donald Trump
a41.title: US President
a41.speech: Declared that the "time for peace" has come; called it a "historic moment for the United States of America, Israel, and the world" and urged Iran to "agree to end this war."

a41.speaker: Iranian officials
a41.name: Iranian officials
a41.speech: Stated that the Fordow facility had been evacuated ahead of time and suffered no irreversible damage.

a41.speaker: Experts (cited by NBC News)
a41.name: Experts (cited by NBC News)
a41.speech: Say the strike on Fordow is unlikely to trigger a nuclear explosion or large-scale radiation release.

a41.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (per The Wall Street Journal)
a41.name: Marco Rubio
a41.title: US Secretary of State (per The Wall Street Journal)
a41.speech: Assured European allies that Washington remained committed to a diplomatic resolution, prior to the strikes.

a41.speaker: Maria Zakharova, Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman
a41.name: Maria Zakharova
a41.title: Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman
a41.speech: Warned the US against military involvement, cautioning that such interference could lead to "truly unpredictable negative consequences."

a41.speaker: Reuters (cited)
a41.name: Reuters (cited)
a41.speech: Reported that the attack involved B-2 strategic bombers previously redeployed to Guam, capable of carrying GBU-57 bunker-buster bombs designed to penetrate heavily fortified underground targets.

a41.speaker: ABC News (cited)
a41.name: ABC News (cited)
a41.speech: Reported that Israel received advance warning of the operation.

a41.speaker: CNN (cited)
a41.name: CNN (cited)
a41.speech: Reported that Trump does not currently plan additional strikes and is awaiting a response from Tehran regarding negotiations.

a41.speaker: The White House
a41.name: The White House
a41.speech: Had indicated a decision on a strike would come within two weeks.

a41.speaker: International observers
a41.name: International observers
a41.speech: Believe the site contained no nuclear warheads or reactors.

a59.speaker: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
a59.name: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
a59.speech: Announced on Saturday that it has successfully shut down more than 11,000 drug shops nationwide and confiscated counterfeit drugs valued in the trillions.

a59.speaker: NAFDAC Director-General (unnamed, referred to as "she")
a59.name: NAFDAC Director-General (unnamed
a59.title: referred to as "she")
a59.speech: Regretted that NAFDAC's findings during the operation have been alarming.

a114.speaker: National Bank of Malawi (NBM) plc
a114.name: National Bank of Malawi (NBM) plc
a114.speech: Has reaffirmed its dedication to maintaining the highest standards in tax compliance following its recent recognition by the Malawi Revenue Authority (MRA), pledging to continue contributing meaningfully to Malawi's economic growth through timely and accurate payment of taxes.

a114.speaker: Daniel Jere, NBM plc Chief Finance Officer
a114.name: Daniel Jere
a114.title: NBM plc Chief Finance Officer
a114.speech: "We are honoured to receive this recognition from MRA. It is a testament to our commitment to fulfilling our tax obligations diligently and on time" ; "It is a reminder that responsible corporate citizenship is not just about profitability, but about active participation in building our nation" ; stressed that tax compliance is one of the bank's core principles and that the recognition serves as a motivating force to uphold and even surpass current standards, noting that NBM plc has consistently posted strong financial results translating into significant tax contributions ; "By paying our taxes, we directly contribute to the development of Malawi, and we will continue to uphold this standard as part of our corporate responsibility" ; "NBM plc pledges to maintain the highest standards in tax compliance, continuing to contribute meaningfully to Malawi's economic growth through timely and accurate payment of taxes."

a114.speaker: Malawi Revenue Authority (MRA)
a114.name: Malawi Revenue Authority (MRA)
a114.speech: Awarded NBM plc a Certificate of Recognition for its outstanding commitment to tax compliance and invaluable contribution to national development, seeking, by recognising compliant institutions, to promote a culture of accountability, responsibility and partnership in national development.

a147.speaker: Government of Kigoma Region
a147.name: Government of Kigoma Region
a147.speech: Said citizens continue to receive water for domestic use from other safe sources while a technical investigation continues into the deaths of fish and other creatures found in the Malagarasi River; after the incident it issued a statement asking citizens to stop fishing or using the water of the Malagarasi River until the investigation is completed.

a147.speaker: Simon Sirro, Ambassador, Regional Commissioner of Kigoma
a147.name: Simon Sirro
a147.title: Ambassador, Regional Commissioner of Kigoma
a147.speech: Said citizens continue to use water from other safe sources and that the government is monitoring whether there is a need to add extra supply of clean and safe water: “You cannot use the water of the Malagarasi River, just as it is even without the problem that has arisen. However, for now the residents of those areas are getting water from other sources because these exist in that area, unlike the Malagarasi River” ; said the government is following the matter closely to identify and take swift action if needed, to ensure citizens do not lack essential water services while the investigation continues.

a147.speaker: Simon Sirro, Ambassador, Regional Commissioner of Kigoma
a147.name: Simon Sirro
a147.title: Ambassador, Regional Commissioner of Kigoma
a147.speech: “The health of our citizens is the first priority. Therefore, we ask all citizens of the areas through which this river passes to follow the instructions given by the experts,” said when he visited the area to see what had happened.

a147.speaker: Some residents of Kigadye Village, Kasulu District
a147.name: Some residents of Kigadye Village
a147.title: Kasulu District
a147.speech: Said they had never witnessed such an event for several decades, while continuing to benefit from various opportunities offered by the river, including water for agriculture, household use and food.

a147.speaker: Nesphory Sugu, Kigoma Regional Sanitation and Environment Officer
a147.name: Nesphory Sugu
a147.title: Kigoma Regional Sanitation and Environment Officer
a147.speech: Said that in cooperation with health experts, a sample of the water in the river was taken for investigation.

a147.speaker: Dr Damas Kayere, Kigoma Regional Medical Officer
a147.name: Dr Damas Kayere
a147.title: Kigoma Regional Medical Officer
a147.speech: Said no one had suffered harm from the incident, but appealed to residents of the area to go to health centres if they experience any effects from using the water or eating fish from the river.

a172.speaker: Dr Danielle Adjafi, President of the CCM-Côte d'Ivoire
a172.name: Dr Danielle Adjafi
a172.title: President of the CCM-Côte d'Ivoire
a172.speech: Congratulated the prize-winner and above all encouraged her to continue in this vein: "Congratulations on the quality of the work that earned you this award. We are proud to know that one of your prize-winning productions concerns the activities of the CCM-CI and especially of the PNOEV. Keep up the good work."

a172.speaker: Paula Hacopian, Côte d'Ivoire portfolio manager at the Global Fund, and Ngalamulume Bibola, PEPFAR Country Coordinator in Côte d'Ivoire
a172.name: Paula Hacopian
a172.title: Côte d'Ivoire portfolio manager at the Global Fund, and Ngalamulume Bibola, PEPFAR Country Coordinator in Côte d'Ivoire
a172.speech: Urged Fatou Sylla always to cover subjects of public interest, in particular those relating to HIV, especially paediatric HIV, which is "a problem in Côte d'Ivoire": "You have our encouragement. We hope for you laurels even better than this one."

a190.speaker: Mamo Mihretu, Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a190.name: Mamo Mihretu
a190.title: Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a190.speech: Candidly addressed the challenges the economy has been grappling with, particularly the inflation rate, which he admitted was aggravated by “uncharacteristically loose” fiscal and monetary policies over the past two years ; “These were deemed necessary to mitigate the impact of the war, drought, and the massive internal displacement,” the Governor said in a press conference at the Central Bank’s headquarters on Sudan Street. “But we’re seeing the consequences.”

a190.speaker: Mamo Mihretu, Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a190.name: Mamo Mihretu
a190.title: Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a190.speech: Maintained that the rate would not decrease total borrowing but merely keep it from ballooning unnecessarily.

a190.speaker: Fiscal and monetary experts
a190.name: Fiscal and monetary experts
a190.speech: Who have long argued for budget discipline and a tighter monetary stance, met the announcements with approval.

a190.speaker: Abdulmenan Mohammed (PhD), London-based financial analyst
a190.name: Abdulmenan Mohammed (PhD)
a190.title: London-based financial analyst
a190.speech: Concurs with a general policy shift towards an interest-based monetary policy framework. He emphasised on political autonomy of the central bank as of first-order importance. Successfully moving past the reserve-prioritising central banking framework requires a simultaneous upgrade to the structural integrity of the institution. The mandatory treasury bond purchases of commercial banks imposed by the central bank contradicted a general orientation towards politically independent central banking, he argued ; “The central bank's independence is crucial for its effectiveness,” he told Fortune ; “It’s a return to a more sensible, stringent fiscal approach. However, while commendable, aiming for a 20pc inflation rate might be a tad optimistic.”

a190.speaker: Abdulmenan Mohammed (PhD), London-based financial analyst
a190.name: Abdulmenan Mohammed (PhD)
a190.title: London-based financial analyst
a190.speech: Warns: “We could see a preference for certain customers, potentially leading to corrupt lending practices.”

a190.speaker: Tewodros Mekonen (PhD), macroeconomist with ties to the London School of Economics
a190.name: Tewodros Mekonen (PhD)
a190.title: macroeconomist with ties to the London School of Economics
a190.speech: Agrees that abandoning the reserve-based orientation in monetary policy requires credible institutions but asserts that development objectives in a poor country can be calibrated by maintaining the transparency of the central bank despite slight nudges from the government. He characterised the new trajectory of the Central Bank as a hybrid of interest and reserve-based monetary policy frameworks ; “While the measures are steps in the right direction, the federal government must exercise caution and avoid viewing the central bank as an open treasury,” he told Fortune.

a190.speaker: Tewodros Mekonen (PhD), macroeconomist with ties to the London School of Economics
a190.name: Tewodros Mekonen (PhD)
a190.title: macroeconomist with ties to the London School of Economics
a190.speech: Argued that despite credit growth over the years, most funds have been absorbed by the public sector through the state-owned behemoth, the Commercial Bank of Ethiopia (CBE) ; “The private sector has been crowded out of the credit market,” he said while indicating that governments are generally inefficient resource allocators.

a190.speaker: Tewodros Mekonen (PhD), macroeconomist with ties to the London School of Economics
a190.name: Tewodros Mekonen (PhD)
a190.title: macroeconomist with ties to the London School of Economics
a190.speech: Summed up the sentiment succinctly: “Consistent application of publicly stated policy garners trust in the market.”

a190.speaker: International community and multilateral financial institutions like the IMF
a190.name: International community and multilateral financial institutions like the IMF
a190.speech: Have consistently advocated for a blend of interest and reserve-based monetary policy frameworks for countries like Ethiopia.

a190.speaker: Sisay Amare, head of the Ethiopian Pulses, Oilseeds & Spices Processors Exporters Association (EPOSPEO)
a190.name: Sisay Amare
a190.title: head of the Ethiopian Pulses, Oilseeds & Spices Processors Exporters Association (EPOSPEO)
a190.speech: Welcomed the forex adjustment. “We’ve been advocating for a change in these,” he told Fortune. “This could mean an uptick in our foreign exchange accounts.” ; While recognising the role of a lower retention rate for exporters in declining forex inflow, he disclosed that too much of it would be spent on importing consumption goods: “Even if the forex surrender rate were zero, the import demand would not be met.”

a190.speaker: Gizat Worku, leading Ethiopian coffee export business figure
a190.name: Gizat Worku
a190.title: leading Ethiopian coffee export business figure
a190.speech: “This is an incentivising move. We’ve already stored export-ready coffee, promising good revenue ahead of the next harvest season.” ; Indicated that several levers and gears would need to be tweaked in productivity and efficiency to tackle the forex woes of a country largely reliant on agricultural produce for its forex earnings.

a190.speaker: Aklilu Wubet, president of Wegagen Bank
a190.name: Aklilu Wubet
a190.title: president of Wegagen Bank
a190.speech: “Inflation has become a formidable challenge for the Ethiopian economy,” he told Fortune. “It’s imperative for banks to rally behind efforts to stabilise our economic landscape.” ; Had expected the move by the Central Bank to limit credit growth and increase interest rates on emergency loans to limit the money supply in the economy: “Excess credit might be fueling inflation.”

a195.speaker: Dr. Hamad Al Kaabi, CEO of Al Ittihad News Center
a195.name: Dr. Hamad Al Kaabi
a195.title: CEO of Al Ittihad News Center
a195.speech: Spoke about the development of podcasting in the Middle East, noting its relatively late adoption compared with Western journalism, but acknowledged its enormous impact, discussed the changing trends of audiences in the region and their search for concise and engaging information, and pointed to the risk of traditional media losing its importance if it does not adapt to their changing expectations.

a195.speaker: Enas Al Rifai, Deputy Managing Editor, The National
a195.name: Enas Al Rifai
a195.title: Deputy Managing Editor, The National
a195.speech: Highlighted the continued influence of radio, which has dominated journalism for decades, and touched on the growing popularity of long-form conversations, where listeners follow engaging dialogue while multitasking; he warned about the danger of echo chambers, stressing the importance of diversity of perspectives for meaningful and balanced conversation.

a195.speaker: Kevin Y. Brown, Head of Content and Strategy, Afripods
a195.name: Kevin Y. Brown
a195.title: Head of Content and Strategy, Afripods
a195.speech: Spoke about the transition from broadcasting to podcasting, particularly in Africa, where radio still plays an essential role, emphasising that podcasting gives listeners the flexibility to access content of their choice at any time while also increasing transparency and trust between presenters and listeners, noting that podcasts have blurred the lines between opinion and reporting and increasingly shape political discourse and public opinion.

a195.speaker: Anup Oommen, Editor, Campaign Middle East
a195.name: Anup Oommen
a195.title: Editor, Campaign Middle East
a195.speech: Drew a comparison between the podcast boom of the early twenty-first century and the revolution of social media platforms, highlighting how they transformed content creation and consumption, and stressed that today's tech-savvy listeners expect to build a connection with programme providers and to have the ability to hold them accountable ; Envisioned a bright future for podcasts, describing them as the foundation of modern media and touching on their power to inform, educate and inspire.

a195.speaker: Participants of the session
a195.name: Participants of the session
a195.speech: Emphasised the transformative power of podcasts as a key vehicle for developing journalism and public interaction, and agreed that podcasts are reshaping how stories are told and also influencing how listeners consume and interact with content.

a215.speaker: Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) studies
a215.name: Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) studies
a215.speech: Show that an increase in firm-level innovation spending raises productivity over time.

a305.speaker: Mathias Gangana, Manager of Southern Programme Influencing and Impact Area (SPIIA), Plan International Ghana
a305.name: Mathias Gangana
a305.title: Manager of Southern Programme Influencing and Impact Area (SPIIA), Plan International Ghana
a305.speech: Disclosed that over 7,000 out-of-school children in 11 districts of three regions have been enrolled in school; said the children were from six districts in North East Region, four districts in Savannah Region and one district in Bono East Region; explained that before enrolment Plan International Ghana recruited volunteer teachers from the communities who took the children through literacy and mathematics for nine months using an abridged lower primary curriculum in their local languages, after which an assessment determined the class they should be enrolled in; said the GEOP was the third such project, adding that between 2013 and 2018, in a project supported by DFID and USAID, they enrolled 5,840 out-of-school children in four districts (Lawra, Nandom, Lambussie and North Gonja), and that in the second project, REACH, implemented between 2015 and 2020, they enrolled 93,315 out-of-school children in 43 districts in five regions; said that after enrolling the children they monitored them for at least two academic years, and that some had become volunteer teachers while others were doing well in other fields; encouraged parents to send their children to school, explaining that without education so many things would be cut away from their children.

a305.speaker: Constant Tchona, Country Director of Plan International Ghana
a305.name: Constant Tchona
a305.title: Country Director of Plan International Ghana
a305.speech: Said they were organising the training within their core values of seeking the well-being of children, their human rights and equality for girls; called on journalists to amplify the voices of children, girls and the communities, to bring to light what was happening and the revolution being led by the people themselves.

a305.speaker: Regina Asamoah, Communications and Influencing Specialist, Plan International Ghana
a305.name: Regina Asamoah
a305.title: Communications and Influencing Specialist, Plan International Ghana
a305.speech: Said the media formed an integral part of what they did and how they got their messages across everywhere they implemented their projects.

a349.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a349.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a349.title: President of South Africa
a349.speech: Expressed on Thursday his "concern" regarding the cuts in US aid to African countries: "We are concerned about the potential impact of the decision by the United States government to suspend some of its funding for HIV and tuberculosis programmes in African countries for 90 days," the president declared during his annual State of the Nation Address (SoNA), stressing that this funding represents around 17% of South African spending on HIV; he stated that the country had managed to provide Treasury funding for HIV and tuberculosis programmes over the years and that the government is considering interventions to respond to immediate needs as well as essential services.

a349.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a349.name: Donald Trump
a349.title: President of the United States
a349.speech: After taking office on 20 January, signed an executive order formalising his country's withdrawal from the World Health Organization, citing "mismanagement" of the coronavirus pandemic and other global health crises, as well as its "failure" to implement urgent reforms and a "lack" of control over excessive political influence by member states.

a349.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a349.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a349.title: President of South Africa
a349.speech: Also stressed that South Africa "stands for a non-racial future": "To fight inequality, we must dismantle the spatial planning of apartheid, which has marked our cities and forced many people to live far from work areas and opportunities," he added.

a349.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a349.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a349.title: President of South Africa
a349.speech: Concerning the deaths of South African soldiers in the east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, announced a week-long period of mourning; specified that 14 soldiers had been killed "in defence of the fundamental right of the Congolese people to live in peace and security", and not "in the pursuit of resources, territory or power" ; "The presence of South African peacekeepers in eastern DRC bears witness to our continued commitment to the peaceful resolution of one of the most intractable conflicts in the world, which has cost millions of lives and displaced millions of people," he declared, calling on all parties to find a peaceful solution.

a349.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a349.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a349.title: President of South Africa
a349.speech: Added that South Africa would continue to promote human rights, peace and friendship as "essential pillars" of its foreign policy, approaching them as the key principles of the 2025 G20 presidency under South African leadership; hosting the G20 for the first time in Africa is an "opportunity to place the needs of Africa and the rest of the global South more firmly on the international development agenda", he concluded.

a353.speaker: Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Government of the Republic of Rwanda (Peace Agreement, preamble)
a353.name: Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Government of the Republic of Rwanda (Peace Agreement
a353.title: preamble)
a353.speech: Reaffirming the mutual commitment to respect the Declaration of Principles signed by the Parties on 25 April 2025, based on mutual respect for sovereignty, territorial integrity, national unity and the peaceful settlement of disputes; recognising the need for a negotiated political resolution - rather than a military solution - to the Parties' disputes; recognising the terms of the Constitutive Act of the African Union, the Charter of the United Nations and UN Security Council resolution 2773 (21 February 2025); taking note of the CONOPS of 31 October 2024 arising from the Luanda process and the communique of the second joint EAC-SADC Summit of 24 March 2025; conscious of the ongoing negotiations between the DRC and the AFC/M23 under the mediation of the State of Qatar in Doha; resolved to prevent a resumption of hostilities, to actively promote lasting peace, stability and integrated economic development throughout the region and to restore normal bilateral relations; determined to promote full respect for human rights and international humanitarian law; they hereby agree to be bound by the provisions that follow.

a353.speaker: Government of the DRC and Government of Rwanda (Peace Agreement, Section 1: Territorial integrity and prohibition of hostilities)
a353.name: Government of the DRC and Government of Rwanda (Peace Agreement
a353.title: Section 1: Territorial integrity and prohibition of hostilities)
a353.speech: The Parties agree to implement the Harmonised Plan for the neutralisation of the FDLR and the disengagement of forces/lifting of Rwanda's defensive measures (CONOPS) of 31 October 2024; agree that disputes shall be settled through processes established by the Agreement rather than through hostilities; agree to refrain from any act of aggression and not to commit, support or tolerate military incursions or other acts, direct or indirect, that threaten the peace and security of the other party or undermine its sovereignty or territorial integrity; agree to allow no military or other hostile activity against one another on or from their respective territories and to provide no support to such activities abroad; the prohibition of hostile acts applies without geographical restriction; the Parties take all possible measures to ensure that all armed groups in the conflict zone cease hostilities; the Parties facilitate the free movement of civilians, including humanitarian personnel, and must respect international humanitarian law.

a353.speaker: Government of the DRC and Government of Rwanda (Peace Agreement, Section 2: Disengagement, disarmament and integration of non-state armed groups)
a353.name: Government of the DRC and Government of Rwanda (Peace Agreement
a353.title: Section 2: Disengagement, disarmament and integration of non-state armed groups)
a353.speech: The Parties support the ongoing negotiations between the DRC and the AFC/M23 with the mediation of the State of Qatar in Doha and efforts to disarm and demobilise non-state armed groups; the Parties immediately and unconditionally cease all State support to non-state armed groups, except to the extent necessary to facilitate implementation of the agreement; they support the disengagement, disarmament and integration of non-state armed groups, including through the P-DDRCS; any eventual reintegration of combatants into the FARDC and the Congolese National Police is to be rigorous, individualised and conditional, case by case, on the basis of clear criteria including physical and moral fitness, respect for and absence of serious violations of international humanitarian law, and loyalty to the State and its institutions.

a353.speaker: Government of the DRC and Government of Rwanda (Peace Agreement, Section 3: Joint Security Coordination Mechanism)
a353.name: Government of the DRC and Government of Rwanda (Peace Agreement
a353.title: Section 3: Joint Security Coordination Mechanism)
a353.speech: The Parties establish and agree to launch, within 30 days of entry into force, a joint security coordination mechanism between the DRC and Rwanda; the mechanism creates common operating procedures and reporting mechanisms to ensure transparency of the scale and scope of operations; it is governed by the irreversible and verifiable end of State support to the FDLR and associated armed groups and the total prohibition of any material, logistical, financial or other support to them; a commitment to identify, assess, locate and neutralise in accordance with the CONOPS of 31 October 2024; a commitment to build on already successful bilateral security cooperation arrangements in which operations are targeted, time-limited and aimed at a specific threat; and the protection of civilians and respect for international humanitarian law.

a353.speaker: Government of the DRC and Government of Rwanda (Peace Agreement, Section 4: Refugees, internally displaced persons and humanitarian considerations)
a353.name: Government of the DRC and Government of Rwanda (Peace Agreement
a353.title: Section 4: Refugees, internally displaced persons and humanitarian considerations)
a353.speech: The Parties, with the support of United Nations agencies, relevant humanitarian organisations and the international community, facilitate the safe, voluntary and dignified return of refugees in a manner consistent with their international legal obligations and with the Tripartite Agreements on the voluntary repatriation of Congolese and Rwandan refugees signed in Kigali on 17 February 2010; recognise the need to end the conflict to allow internally displaced persons to return to their places of origin; and create conditions conducive to the delivery of emergency relief, guaranteeing humanitarian agencies free, safe, unhindered and unconditional access to vulnerable populations, with DRC local authorities responsible under the supervision of the DRC central government.

a353.speaker: Government of the DRC and Government of Rwanda (Peace Agreement, Section 5: MONUSCO and other multilateral support)
a353.name: Government of the DRC and Government of Rwanda (Peace Agreement
a353.title: Section 5: MONUSCO and other multilateral support)
a353.speech: The Parties facilitate and support MONUSCO's capacity to protect civilian populations and implement all elements of its mandate, including by respecting MONUSCO's freedom of movement and taking all appropriate measures to ensure the safety and security of UN personnel deployed in eastern DRC; commit to advancing the implementation of UN Security Council resolution 2773 (2025) and other relevant resolutions; and recognise that MONUSCO, as mandated by resolution 2765 (2024), plays an important role in local peace and security.

a353.speaker: Government of the DRC and Government of Rwanda (Peace Agreement, Section 6: Regional economic integration framework)
a353.name: Government of the DRC and Government of Rwanda (Peace Agreement
a353.title: Section 6: Regional economic integration framework)
a353.speech: The Parties agree to launch, within three months of entry into force, a multi-stage regional economic integration framework to be defined in a separate agreement, building on existing efforts such as the AfCFTA, ICGLR, COMESA and the EAC, in order to develop external trade and investment from the region's critical mineral supply chains and introduce greater transparency; under the framework the Parties launch and/or expand cooperation on shared priorities such as national park management, hydroelectric development, de-risking mineral supply chains, joint management of resources in Lake Kivu, and transparent, formalised end-to-end mineral value chains linking the two countries, in partnership where appropriate with the government and investors of the United States; they commit to explore options for linking the framework to other international or regional economic development initiatives; and they establish or use independent economic audit and anti-corruption mechanisms to monitor mineral supply chains, infrastructure projects and any future economic agreement.

a353.speaker: Government of the DRC and Government of Rwanda (Peace Agreement, Sections 7-9: Implementation, dispute settlement and final provisions)
a353.name: Government of the DRC and Government of Rwanda (Peace Agreement
a353.title: Sections 7-9: Implementation, dispute settlement and final provisions)
a353.speech: Any dispute arising from implementation is to be resolved amicably between the Parties with the facilitation of the Joint Oversight Committee; the Parties hereby create a Joint Oversight Committee and invite, within three days, the African Union Facilitator, Qatar and the United States to sit on it; its mandate is to receive complaints of violations, take measures to remedy violations, monitor and examine accusations and resolve disputes, and it may appoint another representative or establish an ad hoc mechanism; its first meeting is to be held as soon as possible and no later than 45 days after entry into force, with the Parties considering holding it in Washington; the Agreement creates no obligation for non-Party States sitting on the Committee; the Agreement remains in force indefinitely unless otherwise agreed, may be terminated by either Party on sixty (60) days' written notice, may be amended by written agreement, and enters into force upon signature; signed at Washington in 2025 in duplicate in French and English, for the Government of the DRC and the Government of Rwanda, and attested by the Government of the United States of America.

a353.speaker: Government of the DRC and Government of Rwanda (Annex: Modalities of operation of the Joint Security Coordination Mechanism)
a353.name: Government of the DRC and Government of Rwanda (Annex: Modalities of operation of the Joint Security Coordination Mechanism)
a353.speech: The Parties reaffirm their commitment under the terms and obligations of the CONOPS of 31 October 2024 and incorporate it, save as otherwise provided; the JSCM is composed of at least three permanent representatives of each Party, including representatives of the armed forces, intelligence services and foreign affairs ministries; its mission is to identify, assess and locate the FDLR and affiliated groups so as to enable their neutralisation, and it is empowered to monitor implementation of the CONOPS, exchange intelligence and information, define the status and composition of the FDLR, establish and monitor their locations, verify information, coordinate with international actors, assess the threat and coordinate measures to neutralise them; the JSCM meets monthly, alternating between locations in the DRC and Rwanda, adopts terms of reference at its first meeting, drafts a single joint report after each monthly meeting and submits it at ministerial level; the Parties agree to invite the United States and Qatar to attend JSCM meetings as observers and the JSCM may invite other third States or organisations and jointly seek additional financial, logistical and technical support; the JSCM continues to operate until the completion of its mandate.

a353.speaker: Concept of Operations (CONOPS) of the Harmonised Plan for the neutralisation of the FDLR and the disengagement of forces/lifting of Rwanda's defensive measures, Luanda, 31 October 2024
a353.name: Concept of Operations (CONOPS) of the Harmonised Plan for the neutralisation of the FDLR and the disengagement of forces/lifting of Rwanda's defensive measures
a353.title: Luanda, 31 October 2024
a353.speech: States that the DRC and Rwanda have had tense relations for almost three decades which have provoked mutual accusations following the actions of armed groups in eastern DRC; that the African Union mandated the President of the Republic of Angola, His Excellency Joao Manuel Goncalves Lourenco, the AU Champion for peace and reconciliation in Africa, to facilitate dialogue between the DRC and Rwanda; sets out the political objectives (restoring a climate of confidence, creating a safe and secure environment, ensuring lasting peace and stability where human rights are respected, protecting all citizens of both countries and ending hate speech and verbal attacks), the strategic objectives (defeating the FDLR armed group and its auxiliaries, protecting the population and local infrastructure, ensuring the return of displaced persons and controlling natural resource extraction sites), the desired end state, the missions of the DRC (neutralise the FDLR, promote the repatriation of FDLR members to Rwanda, guarantee lasting peace and stability in the Great Lakes sub-region, protect the population and ensure the return of the displaced) and of Rwanda (disengage forces/lift the defensive measures it has put in place and ensure the social reintegration of demobilised and repatriated ex-FDLR combatants), and a four-phase plan of manoeuvre (preparation, conduct of operations, evaluation, stabilisation) with timelines running to D+120, neutralisation and the lifting of Rwanda's defensive measures to be completed within three months; logistical support is the responsibility of each country, which finances its own activities; and it lists the risks and constraints, including the stigmatisation of certain communities, the regionalisation of the conflict, FDLR reprisals against the population, and a lack of political will and mutual trust between Rwanda and the DRC.

a434.speaker: Thabo Qhesi, Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.name: Thabo Qhesi
a434.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.speech: On the likelihood of AGOA being renewed: "This is difficult question because the current US administration is unpredictable. It is unpredictable. I realise that some congress men wanted the renewal but we saw with the executive orders that have been issued by the president there, everything is possible. So, can you imagine? It's difficult to say we can see likelihood of the renewal or not due to uncertainty there."

a434.speaker: Thabo Qhesi, Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.name: Thabo Qhesi
a434.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.speech: On the implications if AGOA is not renewed: "If AGOA is not renewed, we are going to see closure of factories, loss of jobs, both direct and indirect jobs. People tend to focus on the impact of direct jobs, losing the sight that there are a lot of indirect jobs created by this textile. So, they are going to be negatively affected, you know. You talk of public transport, retail, residential property, which are going to be affected, you know. That reality is very true." ; "So, if we can see the closure of the factories, we are going to see the multiplier effects in the entire value chain, which is not healthy for Lesotho."

a434.speaker: Thabo Qhesi, Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.name: Thabo Qhesi
a434.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.speech: On HIV and PEPFAR: "Yes, that is one thing for sure, HIV infections are going to increase because of those risks. Chances are that they are going to increase and the third part in that regard is that PEPFAR which we know is has been supporting health programs, including HIV treatment and prevention, already, the US government has withdrawn the support in that regard. So, yeah, there is that risk again."

a434.speaker: Thabo Qhesi, Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.name: Thabo Qhesi
a434.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.speech: On the government's failure to engage Washington: "one assumes that with this great period of three months, which is going to end on the 8th of July, the government of Lesotho will take an opportunity to mend relations with the US, like we saw with South Africa." ; "South Africa sent a huge team to the US trying to mend the relationship... But so far, I haven't seen the effort of Lesotho trying to engage the US government vigorously. This is my concern, that I haven't seen those efforts or attempts to mend the relationship. Even last week, I was talking to those who were in charge in that sector. Yeah, they were worried that they don't see any effort from the government." ; "Okay, you know, I have tried to engage various people in government. Nobody will give me a concrete answer. Even to those that I talked to, they're also puzzled, you know. They're also puzzled. So, yeah, hopefully, and maybe when the PM, because in the business association, we are still seeking an appointment with the Prime Minister. So, we hope that upon his return from the Spain trip of that FFD4, hopefully, we will get the views of the PM in that regard because these are serious issues."

a434.speaker: Thabo Qhesi, Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.name: Thabo Qhesi
a434.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.speech: On the 50 percent tariff and Lesotho's competitiveness: "Yeah, absolutely. Because remember, we were hit by a 50 percent tariff. So, that 50 percent will take you out of the business. There's no way you can make a profit because when you look at the countries like Kenya, and they are so strong in the textile industry yet they are given 10 percent as opposed to 50 percent." ; "So, clearly, Lesotho would not compete... So, there is no way that we can do business with the US. July 8 is almost a week, next week. I can see a lot of countries laying off employees. It's so uncertain, really. Even this one of reciprocal tariffs, we are still not sure if the US government will maintain that 50 percent or they will make some changes. We are not sure. Like I said, the current US administration is unpredictable."

a434.speaker: Thabo Qhesi, Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.name: Thabo Qhesi
a434.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.speech: On exporting to China: "It won't be easy. It will take time to create new markets. It cannot happen over night because when you look at our neighbours, South Africa, and you look at top 10 countries exporting textile and clothing products to South Africa, China is number one. China is so efficient, they are able to produce a high quality with minimum cost." ; "You cannot compete with China. So, it's highly unlikely that we can see our export going to China. China is interested in raw materials, like wool, mohair and diamond, not particularly the finished product. And we know the finished product; it is where the jobs are being created. Once you transform the raw material, you are creating jobs."

a434.speaker: Thabo Qhesi, Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.name: Thabo Qhesi
a434.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.speech: On what Lesotho should advocate for if AGOA is renewed: "I think we should use Kenya as an example. Kenya will give in 10 percent. Lesotho should advocate getting that 10 percent also. As I get the sentiments of the guys in the industry, they will be comfortable with 10 percent, not 50 percent. So, if AGOA was to be renewed, Lesotho should advocate for 10 percent like their counterparts in East Africa, the likes of Kenya."

a434.speaker: Thabo Qhesi, Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.name: Thabo Qhesi
a434.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.speech: On the relationship between tariffs and AGOA: "Yes, but automatically, those tariffs have impact on AGOA exports. Initially, in AGOA we didnt pay duties. But with these reciprocal tariffs, regardless whether you trade under AGOA, you have to pay those tariffs. That is why some countries opted to negotiate bilaterally with the US government, like South Africa. They really want the automobile products to get into the US market duty-free. Why were they doing that? It's because these reciprocal tariffs are biting."

a434.speaker: Thabo Qhesi, Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.name: Thabo Qhesi
a434.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Private Sector Foundation (Lesotho)
a434.speech: On transition strategies if AGOA is not renewed: "I learnt that shops the likes of Mr Price, Foschini, PicknPay Clothing representatives were here in Lesotho, saying, guys, we heard your case, your situation with the US. We are ready to buy the products from Lesotho because we are impressed with the quality." ; "So I think one of the fallback positions is to explore South African market... So, I think what we have to pay focus on is to explore the South African market. Fortunately, there was a study commissioned by one consultant engaged by LNDC. In that report, we made a recommendation that we should explore collaboration with Tunisia... So there is still a hope that we can do something, if we can put our eggs together."

a434.speaker: Representatives of South African retailers Mr Price, Foschini and PicknPay Clothing (as reported by Thabo Qhesi)
a434.name: Representatives of South African retailers Mr Price
a434.title: Foschini and PicknPay Clothing (as reported by Thabo Qhesi)
a434.speech: Told Lesotho producers: "guys, we heard your case, your situation with the US. We are ready to buy the products from Lesotho because we are impressed with the quality."

a434.speaker: Study commissioned by a consultant engaged by the Lesotho National Development Corporation (LNDC)
a434.name: Study commissioned by a consultant engaged by the Lesotho National Development Corporation (LNDC)
a434.speech: Recommended that Lesotho should explore collaboration with Tunisia, which also exports textiles to South Africa, so that Tunisian producers could manufacture in Lesotho and service the South African market.

a455.speaker: United Nations
a455.name: United Nations
a455.speech: Has issued a warning about the escalating food insecurity crisis in Nigeria’s northeastern region, which is grappling with the devastating impacts of ongoing insurgency.

a455.speaker: UN resident coordinator
a455.name: UN resident coordinator
a455.speech: According to the UN’s resident coordinator, the humanitarian agency is facing critical challenges in securing the necessary funding to address the severe food shortages that threaten to trigger widespread hunger and potentially fatal consequences.

a455.speaker: Mohamed Malick Fall, head of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a455.name: Mohamed Malick Fall
a455.title: head of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a455.speech: Told Reuters that despite Nigeria’s initial commitment of $11 million and another $11 million from the UN’s central pool, reaching the $306 million target was challenging due to hesitancy among international donors: “We are far from where we want to be. That is something we are confronted by even beyond the lean season which is that we have noticed that humanitarian assistance to Nigeria is shrinking” ; expects in the best-case scenario to receive just $300 million, a sharp decrease from the $500 million obtained last year, citing the economic effects of COVID-19 on major donors as the primary cause for the decline ; “Gaza, Ukraine, and Sudan have all emerged in the past two years which makes it difficult to maintain the same pace of funding” ; warns that without immediate intervention, the consequences of food insecurity in Nigeria’s northeast could be “catastrophic” ; “The cost of inaction has many folds with the most pressing being an excess mortality among children.”

a455.speaker: UNICEF data from April (cited)
a455.name: UNICEF data from April (cited)
a455.speech: Indicates that over 120,000 children have already been admitted for treatment of severe acute malnutrition in the region, surpassing the annual target of about 90,000.

a525.speaker: Getrude Imenda, UPND deputy secretary general
a525.name: Getrude Imenda
a525.title: UPND deputy secretary general
a525.speech: Claimed that the opposition political parties are using the Catholic Church and its clerics to fight the government in a bid to remove the UPND from power, singling out Fred Mmembe of the Socialist Party as one of the opposition leaders using the Catholic Church to fight the UPND with the aim of dislodging it from power ; "We have a strong relationship with the Catholic Church. I am sure you saw even the Pope's representative to Zambia reaffirmed that relationship between the government and the church. It's such that leaders like Fred Mmembe are using the church to fight with the government"

a599.speaker: Catholic Diocese of Auchi
a599.name: Catholic Diocese of Auchi
a599.speech: Expressed strong condemnation of the attack and urged swift action to secure the release of the abducted seminarians.

a599.speaker: News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)
a599.name: News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)
a599.speech: According to NAN, the incident occurred around 9pm, sparking fear and renewed concerns over the safety of religious institutions in the state.

a599.speaker: Rev. Fr. Peter Egielewa, Director of Social Communications, Catholic Diocese of Auchi
a599.name: Rev. Fr. Peter Egielewa
a599.title: Director of Social Communications, Catholic Diocese of Auchi
a599.speech: Confirming the attack, described the incident as "deeply saddening" and condemned the repeated targeting of the seminary: "This is the second time in ten months that the school has been attacked" ; "Ten months ago, a priest was kidnapped. Now, three seminarians have been abducted and a civil defence corps officer has been killed, while a local vigilante also sustained gunshot injuries."

a599.speaker: Rev. Fr. Peter Egielewa, Director of Social Communications, Catholic Diocese of Auchi
a599.name: Rev. Fr. Peter Egielewa
a599.title: Director of Social Communications, Catholic Diocese of Auchi
a599.speech: Called on authorities at all levels to take urgent action to protect Catholic institutions and ensure the safety of staff, students, and clergy: "We call on the government to protect the lives of all those who work in Catholic institutions and within our diocese. We hope the security agencies at the local, state, and federal levels will rise to their responsibilities so that our people can live in peace and safety."

a599.speaker: Nigerian government led by President Bola Tinubu
a599.name: Nigerian government led by President Bola Tinubu
a599.speech: Has promised to put an end to the killings and abductions by the rampaging criminals.

a625.speaker: African youth (staged performance at the AFSF 2025 closing ceremony)
a625.name: African youth (staged performance at the AFSF 2025 closing ceremony)
a625.speech: Recalled the urgency of building a united, strong and food-sovereign Africa, highlighting the challenges to be met for an Africa that feeds itself, escaping its food dependency and thereby guaranteeing its dignity; for them their grandparents had always fed Africa without resorting to food imports from other continents, and food sovereignty, far from being an option, is an imperative, because the dignity and cultural identity of the continent are at stake.

a625.speaker: Mabouba Diagne, Senegalese Minister of Agriculture, Food Sovereignty and Livestock
a625.name: Mabouba Diagne
a625.title: Senegalese Minister of Agriculture, Food Sovereignty and Livestock
a625.speech: Said the African continent has two accelerators with which to succeed in its transformation: its youth and technology. He called on African youth to give up the easy criticism about the lack of financing and jobs and to take its destiny into its own hands, because it must no longer be a spectator but a leading actor in the continent's development.

a625.speaker: Amath Pathe Sene, Director of AFSF 2025
a625.name: Amath Pathe Sene
a625.title: Director of AFSF 2025
a625.speech: Giving a brief assessment of the meeting, said that more than a gathering, this Forum had been a journey in the course of which “exceptional young people” allowed their potential and their capacity for innovation to be expressed ; expressed his gratitude to the Senegalese authorities for the successful organisation of the Forum and said the week had been marked by exchanges, panels, exhibitions and numerous trade agreements and partnerships between different actors.

a625.speaker: Jacinthe Anais Myriam Tapsoba, Director of Planning and Monitoring-Evaluation, National Bureau of Major Projects of Burkina (BN-GPB)
a625.name: Jacinthe Anais Myriam Tapsoba
a625.title: Director of Planning and Monitoring-Evaluation, National Bureau of Major Projects of Burkina (BN-GPB)
a625.speech: Said that taking part in the ministerial round table with the technical and financial partners and in other exchange settings made it possible to see what is new elsewhere, to draw inspiration from it, but also to see how to forge partnerships for the development of Burkina Faso's agricultural sector.

a677.speaker: Presidency of the Republic of Cabo Verde
a677.name: Presidency of the Republic of Cabo Verde
a677.speech: According to the Presidency of the Republic, the Head of State also promulgated the Decree-Law establishing the regime of access to the digital inclusion incentive programme designated the "Connect Cabo Verde" Programme, and the Decree-Law establishing the rules for the installation, operation and registration of entities wishing to operate in the Industrial Spaces, the Special Tourist Zones and the Integrated Free Zones under the management of the Maritime Special Economic Zone Authority in São Vicente.

a727.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Liberian Finance Minister
a727.name: Augustine Ngafuan
a727.title: Liberian Finance Minister
a727.speech: Says Liberia is being impacted greatly by the shutdown of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID); named health, education, agriculture, and governance as some key areas that have been affected by the cancellation of USAID projects ; “Before the cancellation of the projects, the entity agreed to scale up its support to 120 million United States Dollars, to enhance education, health, and agriculture in Liberia.” (speaking on the Voice of America)

a727.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Liberian Finance Minister
a727.name: Augustine Ngafuan
a727.title: Liberian Finance Minister
a727.speech: Has disclosed ongoing plans to strengthen domestic revenue generation and ensure value for money in Liberia.

a816.speaker: Chibueze Nwonye, Public Financial Management Specialist of the USAID State2State Activity
a816.name: Chibueze Nwonye
a816.title: Public Financial Management Specialist of the USAID State2State Activity
a816.speech: Said the audit findings on Auditor General Reports was a key interest to the State2State Activity especially in the Education, Health, Water Sanitation and Hygiene sectors in Ebonyi State; maintained that the findings and recommendations made would be beneficial in the implementation of the current budget which he said would lead to proper service delivery.

a816.speaker: Dr Samuel Udu, Ebonyi State Auditor General
a816.name: Dr Samuel Udu
a816.title: Ebonyi State Auditor General
a816.speech: Said while speaking with media that the importance of Audit findings is to ensure accountability, probity and good governance, adding that his office had done a lot to ensure this having worked and handed over to the State House of Assembly through the Public Accounts Committee; maintained that the findings in the field testify the readiness of his office to ensure that the state government get the best accountability records; thanked the State2State Activity which has helped tremendously in preparing an Audit manual which is a guide to audit preparation; explained that audit findings are not for witch hunting, rather it is meant to put audit records straight and use it to correct any seen fault in future auditing.

a816.speaker: Nneka Acholonu Egbuna, Communication Specialist of the USAID State2State Activity
a816.name: Nneka Acholonu Egbuna
a816.title: Communication Specialist of the USAID State2State Activity
a816.speech: Presented communication strategies for rolling out a plan to address the audit findings.

a816.speaker: Hon. Godwin Abiri, Chairman of the Ebonyi State House of Assembly Committee on Public Accounts
a816.name: Hon. Godwin Abiri
a816.title: Chairman of the Ebonyi State House of Assembly Committee on Public Accounts
a816.speech: Thanked State2State Activity for their involvements in improving government’s ability to plan and budget, monitor the budget and be accountable for every item budgeted; said that Ebonyi State has benefited much from the intervention, most importantly the Public Accounts Department.

a837.speaker: Dong Hyun Lee, Country Director of KOICA
a837.name: Dong Hyun Lee
a837.title: Country Director of KOICA
a837.speech: Launching the programme in Koforidua, stressed the critical role being played by ICT in economic growth to facilitate national development ; Citing Korea's example, indicated that in the 1990s, the country's strategic integration of ICT into its educational system laid the foundation for its success ; Stated that Korea's ICT sector had contributed $224 billion in exports, employing over 1.7 billion people ; Added that Korea's deployment journey, which was supported by foreign aid, had inspired the country's commitment to give back to other developing countries such as Ghana, by sharing its expertise in ICT.

a837.speaker: Dong Hyun Lee, Country Director of KOICA
a837.name: Dong Hyun Lee
a837.title: Country Director of KOICA
a837.speech: Highlighted Ghana's potential to bridge its ICT education gap through collaborative efforts and was hopeful that the project would foster long-term positive impact to empower local communities and build self-sufficiency ; Indicated that the first batch of KOICA's volunteers had already been grouped into three teams to ensure its successful implementation.

a837.speaker: Dr Ivy Asantewaa Owusu, Eastern Regional Education Director
a837.name: Dr Ivy Asantewaa Owusu
a837.title: Eastern Regional Education Director
a837.speech: Outlined the importance of Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) education, which, to her, should be prioritised for both individuals and national development.

a837.speaker: Dr Ivy Asantewaa Owusu, Eastern Regional Education Director
a837.name: Dr Ivy Asantewaa Owusu
a837.title: Eastern Regional Education Director
a837.speech: Asked school heads and teachers from the beneficiary schools to actively take part and collaborate effectively with the volunteers to ensure the long-term sustainability of the benefits to be derived ; Stated that the partnership between KOICA and her outfit was a promising step to empower the next generation of Ghanaian students with ICT skills ; Added that by improving infrastructure and providing quality training, it would foster a collaborative learning environment to drive innovation and growth, paving the way for a brighter digital future for the country.

a839.speaker: Nicolau dos Santos, Chairman of the Board (PCA) of RTP (Rádio e Televisão Portuguesa)
a839.name: Nicolau dos Santos
a839.title: Chairman of the Board (PCA) of RTP (Rádio e Televisão Portuguesa)
a839.speech: Opened up opportunities for internships and technical and professional training for TVM workers ; Gave his TVM counterpart guarantees about the possibility of sending TVM technicians for internships and professional training activities at RTP.

a839.speaker: Victor Nhatitima, Chairman of the Board (PCA) of Televisão de Moçambique (TVM)
a839.name: Victor Nhatitima
a839.title: Chairman of the Board (PCA) of Televisão de Moçambique (TVM)
a839.speech: Seeks support in technologies, knowledge and other opportunities for strengthening institutional capacity for the repositioning of TVM in the market.

a839.speaker: Mozambican Football Federation
a839.name: Mozambican Football Federation
a839.speech: Guarantees that it is working, at all costs, for the best of the national team; the position was taken on Thursday during a meeting held with the Ministry of Youth and Sports, Caifadine Manasse.

a839.speaker: Francisco Pagula, Governor of Inhambane
a839.name: Francisco Pagula
a839.title: Governor of Inhambane
a839.speech: Defends the consolidation of the cultural and creative industry as one of the main drivers for boosting tourism and local economic development; he was speaking on Thursday during the reception of the runner-up of the international "Miss World Culture 2025" contest, held in Nigeria.

a839.speaker: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a839.name: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a839.speech: In the speech relaunching the TotalEnergies liquefied natural gas project, said that the act represents Mozambique's capacity to overcome challenges and recover the confidence of international investors.

a839.speaker: Gueta Chapo, First Lady of Mozambique
a839.name: Gueta Chapo
a839.title: First Lady of Mozambique
a839.speech: Appeals for the union of Mozambicans to respond to the needs of families affected by the floods and inundations ; Says the strengthening of cooperation is fundamental to save lives and restore dignity to the victims of calamities.

a839.speaker: Spokesperson of the PRM (Mozambique Republic Police)
a839.name: Spokesperson of the PRM (Mozambique Republic Police)
a839.speech: Said the collapse of an illegal mine that killed five artisanal miners and injured the same number, in the locality of Movinha, Gurúè District, Zambézia Province, happened last Monday.

a839.speaker: Chief Executive of TotalEnergies
a839.name: Chief Executive of TotalEnergies
a839.speech: Announces a donation of 200 million meticais in support of the victims of the floods in the south and centre of the country.

a890.speaker: National Examinations Council of Tanzania (NECTA)
a890.name: National Examinations Council of Tanzania (NECTA)
a890.speech: Confirmed the historic change, which is part of the first nationwide tests to be aligned with the new 2014 Education and Training Policy of 2023 and its revamped curriculum ; also reported that 5,750 pupils with special needs are registered for the assessments, including 1,164 with visual impairment, 111 who are blind, 1,161 with hearing impairment, 1,641 with intellectual disabilities, and 1,673 with physical disabilities.

a890.speaker: Prof Said Mohamed, NECTA Executive Secretary
a890.name: Prof Said Mohamed
a890.title: NECTA Executive Secretary
a890.speech: Announced on Tuesday that the two-day exams begin today, October 22, 2025, with a total of 1,582,140 pupils from 20,517 schools registered for the Standard Four National Assessment (SFNA) ; “For the first time, there will be three optional subjects, which are French, Chinese, and Arabic,” clarifying that each pupil can choose only one of the three new languages.

a890.speaker: Prof Said Mohamed, NECTA Executive Secretary
a890.name: Prof Said Mohamed
a890.title: NECTA Executive Secretary
a890.speech: Explained that to determine an overall pass, the council will consider a pupil’s best-performing subjects, even if they are optional: “The optional languages have increased the number of subjects to nine. To determine the pass level, we will look at the subjects a pupil has performed best in, even if it is an extra subject, and we will include it in the results.”

a1003.speaker: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) report on neglected displacement crises
a1003.name: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) report on neglected displacement crises
a1003.speech: According to a new report from the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC), Cameroon is now the world's most neglected displacement crisis; the annual list is based on three criteria: lack of humanitarian funding, lack of media attention, and a lack of effective political engagement to end conflict and improve conditions for displaced people; the crisis in Ethiopia ranks second, Mozambique third for the first time, Burkina Faso fourth and the Democratic Republic of Congo eighth.

a1003.speaker: Jan Egeland, Secretary General of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a1003.name: Jan Egeland
a1003.title: Secretary General of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a1003.speech: "International solidarity is being overtaken by increasingly introverted and nationalistic policies in previously generous donor nations. This is deepening the neglect of people affected by crisis and displacement at a time when a record number of people have been forced from their homes. Across Europe, the United States and elsewhere we have seen donors turn their backs on people in their hour of need," ; "It is critical that we do not accept donors' abandonment of aid as a foregone conclusion. Displacement isn't a distant crisis: it's a shared responsibility. We must stand up and demand a reversal of brutal aid cuts which are costing more lives by the day."

a1003.speaker: Jan Egeland, Secretary General of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a1003.name: Jan Egeland
a1003.title: Secretary General of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a1003.speech: "Adequate funding is essential. But funding alone cannot halt the suffering. Without effective conflict resolution, disaster prevention and diplomatic engagement, these protracted crises will go on and on. More people will be displaced, and more lives will be shattered."

a1003.speaker: Jan Egeland, Secretary General of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a1003.name: Jan Egeland
a1003.title: Secretary General of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a1003.speech: "The world cannot plead ignorance when it comes to overlooking crises that feature in this report. Each year we warn that things will get worse, and each year that warning becomes a reality. This year I fear that more than ever. With aid budgets being slashed it is down to each and every one of us to stand up and tell global, regional and national politicians to change course, that we will not stand by and let those forced to flee be left behind. What we do this year will be remembered."

a1003.speaker: Djeinabou, 32, a refugee from the Central African Republic living in Cameroon
a1003.name: Djeinabou
a1003.title: 32, a refugee from the Central African Republic living in Cameroon
a1003.speech: "Life is very difficult at times, and we get by with a little farming and working in small businesses to try and find enough to eat. We worry about the future of our children. They need to go to school. We have been forgotten here in Cameroon and it's very difficult for us to even think about the future of our families."

a1003.speaker: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) data
a1003.name: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) data
a1003.speech: The 2024 humanitarian response plan for Cameroon was 45% funded with USD 168.2 million of the USD 371 million required, meaning the funding gap was USD 202.8m; globally in 2024, USD 24.2 billion in funding was received against a total of USD 49.5 billion in requirements, leaving a global funding gap of USD 25.3 billion (51.1%).

a1003.speaker: International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) data
a1003.name: International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) data
a1003.speech: Total military spending for 2024 was USD 2.46 trillion, equal to USD 6.74 billion per day; with the global humanitarian funding gap at USD 25.29 billion, this is equal to 3.7 days, or 1.03%, of global military spending in 2024.

a1003.speaker: Meltwater (media monitoring data)
a1003.name: Meltwater (media monitoring data)
a1003.speech: The displacement crisis in Cameroon was mentioned in 28,800 articles in English, Spanish, French and Arabic in 2024, 15 times fewer than the crisis in Ukraine which was mentioned in 451,000 articles.

a1003.speaker: United States government (via Devex)
a1003.name: United States government (via Devex)
a1003.speech: In January, the United States suspended ongoing aid projects to conduct a foreign assistance review, forcing the majority of US-funded humanitarian work to be put on hold or, eventually, to cease.

a1003.speaker: UK Government
a1003.name: UK Government
a1003.speech: In February, the United Kingdom announced it would be cutting Overseas Development Assistance (ODA) from 0.5% to 0.3% of Gross National Income.

a1003.speaker: Government of the Netherlands
a1003.name: Government of the Netherlands
a1003.speech: In February, the Dutch government also announced a EUR 2.4 billion cut in development aid from 2027.

a1003.speaker: French government (via RFI)
a1003.name: French government (via RFI)
a1003.speech: Announced it would reduce public development assistance by more than EUR 2 billion, close to 40% of its annual funding.

a1003.speaker: Swiss, Swedish, German and Belgian governments (via Devex, SwissInfo, Development Today)
a1003.name: Swiss
a1003.title: Swedish, German and Belgian governments (via Devex, SwissInfo, Development Today)
a1003.speech: Have also announced cuts in aid assistance budgets.

a1022.speaker: Bill Gates, billionaire philanthropist and Microsoft co-founder
a1022.name: Bill Gates
a1022.title: billionaire philanthropist and Microsoft co-founder
a1022.speech: Pledged on Thursday to give his entire fortune away over the next 20 years to support global health initiatives; said he will donate "virtually all" his wealth through the Gates Foundation ; "There are too many urgent problems to solve for me to hold onto resources that could be used to help people" ; "That is why I have decided to give my money back to society much faster than I had originally planned" ; said he expects the foundation to spend more than $200 billion (175.8 billion euros) through 2045.

a1022.speaker: Gates Foundation
a1022.name: Gates Foundation
a1022.speech: Said this would double its current spending levels, and that while the organisation's overall priorities aren't changing, it will home in on three key goals: curbing preventable deaths among mothers and babies, addressing lethal infectious diseases, and lifting "millions of people out of poverty."

a1022.speaker: One analysis (cited)
a1022.name: One analysis (cited)
a1022.speech: Found that without the US's roughly $12 billion (10.6 billion euros) in spending on global health in 2024, roughly 25 million people could die over the next 15 years from HIV, tuberculosis (TB), maternal health complications, and in early childhood.

a1022.speaker: United Nations' AIDS agency (UNAIDS)
a1022.name: United Nations' AIDS agency (UNAIDS)
a1022.speech: Said earlier this week that it would cut its workforce by more than half and move remaining staffers to cheaper posts in response to drastic budget cuts from donors.

a1278.speaker: Elon Musk, billionaire and Trump adviser
a1278.name: Elon Musk
a1278.title: billionaire and Trump adviser
a1278.speech: has falsely accused USAID of being a "criminal" organisation.

a1278.speaker: Steve Schmida, co-founder of Vermont-based Resonance, a USAID contractor
a1278.name: Steve Schmida
a1278.title: co-founder of Vermont-based Resonance, a USAID contractor
a1278.speech: "We had millions of dollars in invoices due to be paid that had been approved by our clients in the US government. We quickly understood that this was a serious threat to our business." ; He began laying off and furloughing dozens of his staff as he calculated that about 90 per cent of his revenue was about to disappear. He said that once he is done, all but about a dozen of his nearly 100 US-based employees will have been impacted. ; "The last 10 days have been the worst 10 days of my professional life." ; He said he might have to go to court over the outstanding balances.

a1278.speaker: An official at a USAID implementing partner (anonymous, spoke on condition of anonymity due to fear of retribution)
a1278.name: An official at a USAID implementing partner (anonymous
a1278.title: spoke on condition of anonymity due to fear of retribution)
a1278.speech: said the company had to furlough hundreds of US-based staff, many of whom were owed over $50 million by the US government in invoices from November and December that are past due; said they might have to go to court over the outstanding balances.

a1278.speaker: Rose Zulliger, former senior malaria technical advisor with the President's Malaria Initiative, USAID contractor
a1278.name: Rose Zulliger
a1278.title: former senior malaria technical advisor with the President's Malaria Initiative, USAID contractor
a1278.speech: "It's not just the personal stress of I've lost my job… It's also the reality that global health as we know it, and the work that we do, saving lives and also protecting Americans. Our work has been put on pause, and the trust and relationships that we have worked so hard (for), that are so integral to the US influence in the global sphere, have all been ruptured."

a1278.speaker: Esther Zeledon, part-time institutional support contractor for USAID
a1278.name: Esther Zeledon
a1278.title: part-time institutional support contractor for USAID
a1278.speech: said she and her husband lost 95 per cent of their income as a result of Mr Trump's executive orders targeting foreign assistance and diversity measures; they are unsure if they will have to move in with her parents in a couple of months and have been discussing measures such as taking money from their 401(k) retirement plan. "It's horrible because we had planned our entire year with our finances… there's so much uncertainty."

a1278.speaker: Amanda Satterwhite, USAID independent contractor
a1278.name: Amanda Satterwhite
a1278.title: USAID independent contractor
a1278.speech: said she isn't certain how she and her husband will make their mortgage payments and she has already begun looking for a new job because "no one is sure in what state the aid industry is going to return."

a1278.speaker: Many USAID staff and contractors
a1278.name: Many USAID staff and contractors
a1278.speech: have expressed shock at how quickly the administration moved to fire people only a few days before their benefits and health insurance expired.

a1325.speaker: Africa CDC and WHO (Joint Continental Response Plan)
a1325.name: Africa CDC and WHO (Joint Continental Response Plan)
a1325.speech: Have updated their Joint Continental Response Plan for the mpox emergency as the disease continues to affect new areas; the revised strategy focuses on controlling outbreaks, while expanding vaccination coverage and transitioning toward a longer-term, sustainable response ; the updated joint plan calls for intensified efforts to bring outbreaks under control, while also taking concrete actions to integrate mpox into routine health services.

a1325.speaker: Africa CDC
a1325.name: Africa CDC
a1325.speech: Declared a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security in August 2024 after the clade Ib strain began spreading through sexual networks, within households and through close contact.

a1325.speaker: WHO Director-General
a1325.name: WHO Director-General
a1325.speech: Declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in August 2024.

a1325.speaker: WHO
a1325.name: WHO
a1325.speech: Has also updated the global strategic plan to curb - and where feasible, to stop - human-to-human transmission of mpox; the joint continental plan is aligned with the global strategy.

a1325.speaker: Africa CDC and WHO (source of report data)
a1325.name: Africa CDC and WHO (source of report data)
a1325.speech: Reported that vaccination efforts are underway, with more than 650,000 doses administered in 6 countries, 90% of which have been administered in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and over a million doses delivered to 10 countries ; that diagnostic testing capacity in the DRC has grown from 2 laboratories in late 2023 to 23 laboratories in 12 provinces today ; that ongoing conflict and insecurity in eastern DRC, as well as humanitarian aid cuts, continue to limit the public health response and restrict access to essential services, and that across countries and partners over US$220 million is needed to fill funding gaps for the mpox response ; that in the first two months of 2025, 60 countries reported mpox, with the majority of cases and deaths reported from the African continent.

a1346.speaker: Department for Disaster Management Affairs (Dodma), Malawi
a1346.name: Department for Disaster Management Affairs (Dodma)
a1346.title: Malawi
a1346.speech: Has disclosed that it is yet to raise the full amount of the resources required for the El Nino response, with the shortfall standing at $48 million (about K73.5 billion).

a1346.speaker: Fyabupi Mwafongo, Dodma deputy director
a1346.name: Fyabupi Mwafongo
a1346.title: Dodma deputy director
a1346.speech: Said Dodma is yet to raise the full amount of the $446 million required for the El Nino response. He, however, said 78 percent of the required funds have been raised. ; "Specifically, for the food security cluster, the requirement was $197 million. So far, 78 percent of the needed funds have been raised, but there remains a $42 million shortfall to fully meet the demand."

a1346.speaker: Jae Kyung Park, Korean Ambassador to Malawi
a1346.name: Jae Kyung Park
a1346.title: Korean Ambassador to Malawi
a1346.speech: Expressed satisfaction with the way WFP has used the funds and hinted at supporting more programmes that promote resilience among communities impacted by disasters. ; "Natural disasters are unpredictable, but if further disasters occur, Korea is ready and willing to provide more assistance. However, it is also important to prepare for the worst while hoping for the best. The focus should be on adapting to climate change impacts and providing sustainable development assistance."

a1346.speaker: Simon Denhere, World Food Programme country manager for Malawi
a1346.name: Simon Denhere
a1346.title: World Food Programme country manager for Malawi
a1346.speech: Asked if the aftermath of Cyclone Jude will affect the El Nino response plan, said no major changes are expected. ; "WFP works closely with the Government of Malawi to anticipate disasters and respond accordingly. Preparations were already made, and a WFP team is currently in Blantyre and other districts in the South, monitoring the situation. If intervention is needed, WFP is ready to respond."

a1346.speaker: Simon Denhere, World Food Programme country manager for Malawi
a1346.name: Simon Denhere
a1346.title: World Food Programme country manager for Malawi
a1346.speech: Explained that the El Nino response has been going on well despite challenges, including the coinciding of the lean season with the cyclone season, which stretches resources as WFP shifts from assisting people affected by the lean season to those impacted by cyclones; he hailed Dodma for leading the response which will see WFP assisting 2.1 million people, with 90 percent of the target already reached.

a1587.speaker: Hippolyte Fofack, fellow with the Sustainable Development Solutions Network at Columbia University (commentary provided by Project Syndicate)
a1587.name: Hippolyte Fofack
a1587.title: fellow with the Sustainable Development Solutions Network at Columbia University (commentary provided by Project Syndicate)
a1587.speech: writes that despite the disproportionate impact of the aid cuts on the continent, some Africans see the demise of foreign aid as an opportunity; argues that in the wake of Trump's assault on USAID, Africa should put itself on a path toward health self-sufficiency, take more control over the response to HIV/AIDS and malaria from research and development to manufacturing diagnostics and treatments, and that "The continent needs fair trade, not aid"; argues pooling resources and achieving economies of scale through the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) could crowd in private capital, and that "Trump's attack on development assistance can be the wake-up call African leaders need" and "the end of USAID could galvanise African governments to confront their countries' challenges head-on."

a1587.speaker: Uhuru Kenyatta, then-Kenyan President
a1587.name: Uhuru Kenyatta
a1587.title: then-Kenyan President
a1587.speech: warned the pan-African Parliament about the dangers of development assistance in 2015; he did not want the continent's future left to the good graces of outside interests. He argued that foreign aid, which often comes with terms and conditions that preclude progress, should not be an acceptable basis for prosperity and freedom. He urged, it was time to give it up.

a1587.speaker: Afrobarometer survey of 34 African countries
a1587.name: Afrobarometer survey of 34 African countries
