a1587.speech: found that 65pc of respondents wanted their governments to finance development with their own resources, rather than with external loans.

a1587.speaker: Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana's first president and a co-founder of the Organisation of African Unity
a1587.name: Kwame Nkrumah
a1587.title: Ghana's first president and a co-founder of the Organisation of African Unity
a1587.speech: viewed the foreign-aid system as a form of neocolonialism.

a1587.speaker: John D. Mahama, Ghanaian President
a1587.name: John D. Mahama
a1587.title: Ghanaian President
a1587.speech: calling the destruction of USAID "a signal to Africa that the time has come for us to be more self-reliant."

a1587.speaker: Development professionals in Western capitals
a1587.name: Development professionals in Western capitals
a1587.speech: warn that a humanitarian catastrophe will soon unfold on the continent.

a1587.speaker: Nicholas Enrich, formerly USAID's acting assistant administrator for global health
a1587.name: Nicholas Enrich
a1587.title: formerly USAID's acting assistant administrator for global health
a1587.speech: According to Enrich, gutting the agency would result in an additional 71,000 to 166,000 deaths a year from malaria and one million children annually with untreated severe acute malnutrition, among other harmful consequences.

a1587.speaker: A 2023 study
a1587.name: A 2023 study
a1587.speech: has shown that foreign aid tends to weaken fiscal capacity in African democracies.

a1612.speaker: Federal Executive Council (FEC) of Nigeria
a1612.name: Federal Executive Council (FEC) of Nigeria
a1612.speech: Approved N4.8 billion to support HIV treatment programmes in Nigeria in response to the ongoing uncertainty surrounding US HIV funding, and an additional N1.07 billion to finance healthcare sector reforms under the Human Capital Opportunities for Prosperity and Equity (HOPE) programme.

a1612.speaker: Health experts
a1612.name: Health experts
a1612.speech: Have commended the move but warn that sustained financial commitment and efficient resource allocation will be crucial for its long-term impact.

a1612.speaker: Nigerian government
a1612.name: Nigerian government
a1612.speech: Announced plans to retain 28,000 health workers whose salaries were previously covered by USAID, whose activities have been halted by US President Donald Trump, as part of efforts to reduce Nigeria's reliance on foreign aid and take charge of its healthcare system.

a1612.speaker: Nigerian government
a1612.name: Nigerian government
a1612.speech: Announced in February that over 12 million Nigerian girls have been immunised against cervical cancer as part of the country's expanded vaccination programme.

a1612.speaker: Health officials
a1612.name: Health officials
a1612.speech: Have emphasised the need to sustain vaccination efforts, particularly in rural areas where access to immunisation remains limited.

a1612.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a1612.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a1612.speech: According to WHO, Nigeria recorded 12,000 cases and 8,000 deaths from cervical cancer in 2020.

a1612.speaker: PREMIUM TIMES (report)
a1612.name: PREMIUM TIMES (report)
a1612.speech: Published a report in February highlighting the dire healthcare challenges faced by Nigerians with albinism, many of whom die prematurely due to lack of access to skin cancer treatment; three to five persons with albinism die of skin cancer every six months, and only two per cent survive to reach the age of 40.

a1612.speaker: Experts (on albinism care)
a1612.name: Experts (on albinism care)
a1612.speech: Stress the urgent need for government intervention and the inclusion of albinism-related care in universal health coverage plans.

a1612.speaker: Health experts (on the retirement age increase)
a1612.name: Health experts (on the retirement age increase)
a1612.speech: Have lauded the move to raise the retirement age for doctors and healthcare workers from 60 to 65 years, noting that it will help curb the mass exodus of Nigerian doctors seeking better opportunities abroad.

a1612.speaker: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC)
a1612.name: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC)
a1612.speech: Reported a continued surge in Lassa fever infections, with 290 confirmed cases and 53 deaths recorded in four weeks ; noted that the national Lassa fever multi-partner, multi-sectoral incident management system has been activated to coordinate response at all levels at the Emergency Operation Centre (EOC).

a1612.speaker: Nigerian Institute of Medical Research (NIMR)
a1612.name: Nigerian Institute of Medical Research (NIMR)
a1612.speech: Has raised concerns over the increasing prevalence of emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases in Nigeria, particularly Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers (VHFs); the institute emphasised the urgent need for enhanced disease surveillance, improved diagnostics, and increased public awareness to curb the spread of these infections.

a1612.speaker: Trump administration
a1612.name: Trump administration
a1612.speech: Disclosed plans to slash USAID's foreign assistance budget by 92 per cent, significantly reducing the agency's ability to support development efforts in countries like Nigeria.

a1612.speaker: USAID (the agency)
a1612.name: USAID (the agency)
a1612.speech: Said that the contract and foreign assistance programmes to be eliminated total $54 billion; said the slash in the USAID programme is part of a review to significantly reduce US foreign assistance to countries.

a1720.speaker: Brian Chituwo, Zambian Minister of Science and Technology
a1720.name: Brian Chituwo
a1720.title: Zambian Minister of Science and Technology
a1720.speech: Said the bill was needed because GMOs were bound to find their way into Zambia.

a1720.speaker: George Kunda, Zambian Minister of Justice
a1720.name: George Kunda
a1720.title: Zambian Minister of Justice
a1720.speech: Said the Zambian government was eager to have the bill passed and made into law to allow for the domestication of the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety, to which Zambia is a signatory ; said Zambia needs the legislation to avoid becoming a 'dumping ground' for such products, as it currently does not have the technology to test imported material for GMOs.

a1720.speaker: Saviour Chishimba, chairperson of the Parliamentary Committee on Education, Science and Technology
a1720.name: Saviour Chishimba
a1720.title: chairperson of the Parliamentary Committee on Education, Science and Technology
a1720.speech: "The bill is aimed at ensuring that Zambia remains a GMO free country."

a1738.speaker: Adebayo Adelabu, Minister of Power
a1738.name: Adebayo Adelabu
a1738.title: Minister of Power
a1738.speech: Said the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) will need about N2.779 trillion to execute its 149 projects scattered across the country, noting that the ministry's total budget falls short of this amount and emphasising the need for cooperation and collaboration to achieve the president's mandate for improved electricity supply: "For the TCN alone, we will need about N2.779 trillion to enable us to execute the about 149 projects we are currently engaged in all over the country. Our total budget as a ministry is not even up to this but as the saying goes that half bread is better than none." ; "I'm telling you so that you can be aware of the kind of money that is needed in the ministry for us to address our electricity challenges. We need your cooperation and collaboration in achieving the mandate of Mr President in electricity supply to Nigerians."

a1738.speaker: Bolaji Tunji, Special Adviser on Strategic Communication and Media Relations to the Minister of Power (statement)
a1738.name: Bolaji Tunji
a1738.title: Special Adviser on Strategic Communication and Media Relations to the Minister of Power (statement)
a1738.speech: Disclosed in a statement on Tuesday that the minister made the remarks when he appeared before the two chambers at the National Assembly for the ministry's budget presentation on Monday.

a1738.speaker: Adebayo Adelabu, Minister of Power
a1738.name: Adebayo Adelabu
a1738.title: Minister of Power
a1738.speech: Revealed that when he was appointed generation was just about 4,100 megawatts and within a year capacity increased by over 1,000 megawatts: "We reached a maximum capacity of 5270 megawatts. The improvements in generation capacity were due to improvements in the operation of existing power plants and the commissioning of new plants. This boost was partly driven by efforts to ensure more efficient use of existing infrastructure and completion of some power projects."

a1738.speaker: Adebayo Adelabu, Minister of Power
a1738.name: Adebayo Adelabu
a1738.title: Minister of Power
a1738.speech: Said approval had been given for the commencement of the second phase of the Siemens power project under the Presidential Power Initiative with 95 per cent completion of the pilot stage in 2024, and that the project will energise power supply through the construction of five substations and permanently address grid collapse: "The federal government is fully determined to address these challenges and issues that have been blocking our progress in our effort to provide electricity to Nigerians and our consumers. Of particular note is the grid collapse, which concerns the obsolete equipment around our power stations." ; "We have almost concluded the take off of the project and it will involve building five substations across the country. This will energise our supply so that the issue of grid collapse will be a thing of the past. By next week, we will begin the contracts for the substations to come on board."

a1738.speaker: Adebayo Adelabu, Minister of Power
a1738.name: Adebayo Adelabu
a1738.title: Minister of Power
a1738.speech: Informed the lawmakers of the need to address vandalism of electricity assets: "One other critical thing I want to draw your attention to is the issue of vandalisation as it concerns our assets. It is important we sensitise our people against this act. We must be involved in serious advocacy on this issue. We must jointly address the issue of protecting the power assets. A damage to one is damage to all, especially the transmission assets; they are so interwoven, and damage to one is damage to all." ; "In this case, we need the cooperation and collaboration of all our security agencies, the Army, the Air Force, the Navy, the Police and the Civil Defence. But more importantly, we need the cooperation and collaboration of the office of the National Security Adviser. We are not just dealing with those who steal cables but bandits who use dynamite to blow up towers and transmission lines." ; said no amount can be voted for this either as a ministry or in TCN that can solve this ; "Our transmission line from Shiroro-Mando-Kaduna which was attacked by these bandits, and which we are yet to put back, was done in a manner as if we were in a war situation. We did not budget for what was spent to put what we could together. How do we manage the protection of these assets? This must be our joint concern, so we are calling for your cooperation and collaboration in addressing this security challenge facing us in our power assets."

a1738.speaker: Adebayo Adelabu, Minister of Power
a1738.name: Adebayo Adelabu
a1738.title: Minister of Power
a1738.speech: Noted that the federal government is ready to address the issues hindering the electricity sector in 2025: "We hope the year will be a better one for us in the ministry. As I said before, I want to reiterate that we will focus on this Presidential Power Initiative in ensuring that our grid is stable and does not suffer collapse and when it does, within the very shortest time, it is restored and brought back on board."

a1738.speaker: Adebayo Adelabu, Minister of Power
a1738.name: Adebayo Adelabu
a1738.title: Minister of Power
a1738.speech: Disclosed that the ministry will work with local contractors in their procurement plans for the year: "I also want to let you know that we are encouraging our local contractors in providing our materials such as cables, poles and so on. This will help us to conserve our foreign exchange and reduce the transaction cycles we often face while we import. This will save us time in our procurement this year."

a1772.speaker: Watson Institute for International & Public Affairs (report)
a1772.name: Watson Institute for International & Public Affairs (report)
a1772.speech: Published a report highlighting the colossal aid the United States provides to Israel, showing that the US government spent at least $22.76 billion on military aid to Israel between 7 October 2023 and 30 September of this year: about $17.9 billion on direct military aid to Israel and $4.86 billion on American military operations in the war zone, including actions against Houthi forces in Yemen, such as the deployment of aircraft carriers and air defence batteries in the region.

a1772.speaker: Bank of Israel (official estimates)
a1772.name: Bank of Israel (official estimates)
a1772.speech: According to official estimates from the Bank of Israel, the total cost of the war would amount to about 250 billion shekels ($65 billion), of which approximately 118 billion shekels ($31 billion) is for military costs, including the army's operational costs, the resupply of military equipment, ammunition and logistical support.

a1772.speaker: Watson Institute study (document cited)
a1772.name: Watson Institute study (document cited)
a1772.speech: The study stresses that the colossal sum already approved was only a first step, that according to the study the Pentagon has updated the delivery dates for these systems to between 2026 (mortar shells) and 2029 (for the F-15s), and the document stresses that Israel is the country that has received the most American aid since the Second World War, $251.2 billion over 66 years, and that the aid provided by the Biden administration to Israel over the past year was the highest in the history of relations between the two countries, 25% higher than the second largest amount — $14 billion at the end of the 1970s.

a1772.speaker: Biden administration
a1772.name: Biden administration
a1772.speech: On 13 August, the Biden administration announced additional arms contracts worth $20.3 billion, including the sale of Boeing F-15 fighter jets; the package includes 50 F-15 fighter jets ($18.8 billion), more than 32,000 rounds of tank ammunition ($774 million), tactical vehicles ($583 million), 30 advanced medium-range air-to-air missiles ($102 million) and 50,000 mortar shells ($61 million).

a1825.speaker: Prof. Amadou Keïta, Malian Minister of Mines
a1825.name: Prof. Amadou Keïta
a1825.title: Malian Minister of Mines
a1825.speech: Said that in 2023 Mali chose to adopt a new mining code and, for the first time in its history, a law on local content, major reforms that are part of an overall vision of the refoundation of the State and that stem from a strong aspiration of the Malian people expressed during the National Refoundation Conference ; said the implementing decrees of the Mining Code and of the local content law were adopted in July 2024, that the time has not yet come to draw up an assessment, but "we hope that when they are applied in their full scope, Mali will be able to pride itself on a mining sector fully integrated into the national economy and capable of driving development" ; stressed that several mining companies, after negotiations, are preparing to migrate to the 2023 code and are all committing to apply the local content measures.

a1825.speaker: Prof. Amadou Keïta, Malian Minister of Mines
a1825.name: Prof. Amadou Keïta
a1825.title: Malian Minister of Mines
a1825.speech: On SOREM, said the criticism of a slow start "does not always take into account the overall context and the actions under way"; said the state-owned company, created in August 2022, embodies the firm determination of the President of the Transition, Colonel Assimi Goïta, to put the State back at the heart of research, exploitation and marketing of mining products; said making it operational is one of the Ministry's priorities, that it held the second session of its board on 25 July 2024 and has just been granted a gold exploration permit over the N'Tahaka perimeter of 97.41 km² in the N'Tillit Circle in Gao; said the Morila mine will come back under SOREM's control to ensure continuity of operation after difficulties caused by "the misconduct of its previous operator," that the other mining assets belonging to that Australian company will also revert to SOREM, and that the State intends to provide SOREM with adequate resources.

a1825.speaker: Prof. Amadou Keïta, Malian Minister of Mines
a1825.name: Prof. Amadou Keïta
a1825.title: Malian Minister of Mines
a1825.speech: On the gold refinery project, said it is one dimension of the partnership with Russia in the mining sector and "a decisive turning point in the organisation and management of this sector"; said "the final objective of this process is that all the gold produced on Malian territory be refined in Mali under optimal conditions"; said the State has made available 10 hectares for the refinery, has a preliminary design plan, specifications and the elements needed for a feasibility study, and that regular follow-up is carried out with the Russian partner so that Mali may have, after more than 60 years of gold mining, a refinery meeting international standards.

a1825.speaker: Prof. Amadou Keïta, Malian Minister of Mines
a1825.name: Prof. Amadou Keïta
a1825.title: Malian Minister of Mines
a1825.speech: On the renegotiated Goulamina lithium contract, congratulated the government of Mali on the agreement and on the project, "one of the biggest lithium projects in Africa and in the world," saying it reflects the diversification policy advocated for the country's mineral resources; said a first estimate indicates an increase in the State budget of about 100 billion CFA francs per year, that the project will bring additional contributions to financing development of the mining, energy, infrastructure and transport sectors and local development, with a minimum of 250 billion CFA francs in turnover expected for local subcontractors and considerable job creation in the Bougouni region; recalled that the mine is operated by the Chinese partner Ganfeng Lithium Co and that Mali will set up a spodumene plant starting production before the end of 2024.

a1825.speaker: Prof. Amadou Keïta, Malian Minister of Mines
a1825.name: Prof. Amadou Keïta
a1825.title: Malian Minister of Mines
a1825.speech: On State oversight of the exploitation chain, said this is an undertaking that extends to all mining companies operating in Mali, that the mining administration has the obligation to ensure fair exploitation of resources and that the new mining code directs all services of the Ministry of Mines and other ministerial departments to strictly control mining activity; said the State must give itself the means to monitor mining companies both on the real value of exports and on compliance with all provisions of their activities, notably environmental standards, which is the point of the institutional reform being undertaken.

a1825.speaker: Prof. Amadou Keïta, Malian Minister of Mines
a1825.name: Prof. Amadou Keïta
a1825.title: Malian Minister of Mines
a1825.speech: On the cancellation of the Tassiga manganese exploitation permit, said "our objective is not to proceed with cancellations of mining titles," as that creates periods of uncertainty for the mine's value chain, from workers to subcontractors and neighbouring communities; said that in any event it is the administration's responsibility to ensure compliance with the laws in force in the Republic of Mali and that when serious breaches in the agreement binding the State to a mining company are established, the law must be applied in all its rigour; said that on the Tassiga mine, awarded to Metal Mass PTY Ltd since July 2011, the administration identified facts, some of which called for immediate cancellation of the permit without formal notice, and that "we intend to uphold the interests of the State and of our people."

a1825.speaker: Prof. Amadou Keïta, Malian Minister of Mines
a1825.name: Prof. Amadou Keïta
a1825.title: Malian Minister of Mines
a1825.speech: On fraudulent gold exports and lost State revenue, said there are three legal regimes for gold exploitation in Mali under the Mining Code — large-scale mining, small-scale mining and artisanal gold mining — and that any exploitation outside this framework is illegal, with very precise penalties; specified that "our framework is being strengthened with the prospect of creating a special mining brigade and a Police Commission responsible for mining activities," two bodies tasked with cracking down on violations of mining legislation, plus a third body dedicated to supervising artisanal mining; reiterated "the government's full commitment to cleaning up the mining sector, through an in-depth review of the mining cadastre but also through collegial work of control and, where appropriate, enforcement."

a1825.speaker: Prof. Amadou Keïta, Malian Minister of Mines
a1825.name: Prof. Amadou Keïta
a1825.title: Malian Minister of Mines
a1825.speech: On major actions planned, said the reform must be completed by a resizing of certain services of the Ministry of Mines, starting with the National Directorate of Geology and Mines (DNGM), to give them the capacity required by the 2023 Mining Code and the local content law; said "we remain fully committed to the complete launch of SOREM," which will take form with the forthcoming resumption of activities at the Morila mine and the start of exploration at N'Tahaka, and that close monitoring of mines in difficulty will be maintained to preserve jobs and ensure optimal overall production.

a1877.speaker: African Guarantee Fund (AGF) (announcement)
a1877.name: African Guarantee Fund (AGF) (announcement)
a1877.speech: announced the launch of its Mission 300 Local Currency Guarantee Facility, a groundbreaking initiative to mobilize $5 billion to support energy access projects across Africa, targeting financing for small and medium-sized enterprises in the Distributed Renewable Energy sector.

a1877.speaker: Wale Shonibare, Director for Energy Financial Solutions, Policy and Regulations at the African Development Bank
a1877.name: Wale Shonibare
a1877.title: Director for Energy Financial Solutions, Policy and Regulations at the African Development Bank
a1877.speech: said: “The Mission 300 Local Currency Guarantee Facility will encourage collaboration with African governments whilst leveraging concessional financing from the African Development Bank, the World Bank Group, and other development partners to scale the involvement of local banks in financing Distributed Renewable Energy solutions.”

a1877.speaker: Jules Ngankam, AGF Group CEO
a1877.name: Jules Ngankam
a1877.title: AGF Group CEO
a1877.speech: said: “AGF’s leadership in driving financial innovation for SMEs aligns seamlessly with the goals of Mission 300. By addressing financing gaps and fostering public-private partnerships, AGF plays a crucial role in driving inclusive energy solutions, accelerating the energy transition, and reducing carbon emissions across the continent.” ; “We have successfully implemented the Green Guarantee, which has facilitated progress toward national commitments under the Africa Energy Declaration, the African Union’s Vision 2063, and the global Sustainable Development Goals, fostering inclusive growth and climate resilience.”

a1940.speaker: Sir Gavin Williamson, British Conservative Party MP
a1940.name: Sir Gavin Williamson
a1940.title: British Conservative Party MP
a1940.speech: Has renewed calls for the United States to recognize Somaliland following his accusations that the Somali government has misused USAID funds to support Al-Shabaab militants. In a statement on X (formerly Twitter) on Sunday, welcomed the US decision to suspend USAID funding, claiming that Somali authorities were channeling funds to the militant group. "Somalia, through Al-Shabaab, has been sending arms and resources to the Houthis. Donald Trump was right to strike Somalia. Now is the time to recognize Somaliland, the one democratic nation in the region, and stop propping up the terrorist-supporting Mogadishu regime with US dollars."

a1940.speaker: Sir Gavin Williamson, British Conservative Party MP
a1940.name: Sir Gavin Williamson
a1940.title: British Conservative Party MP
a1940.speech: Also commented on the recent US airstrikes targeting ISIS militants in Puntland, commending the move and calling for a shift in US policy.

a1940.speaker: Office of the Somali President
a1940.name: Office of the Somali President
a1940.speech: Said President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud was informed of the airstrike.

a1940.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a1940.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a1940.title: President of Somalia
a1940.speech: Wrote on X that he extended his deepest gratitude for "the unwavering support of the United States in our shared fight against terrorism." ; "Your bold and decisive leadership, Mr. President, in counterterrorism efforts is highly valued and welcomed in Somalia."

a2058.speaker: Harouna Cissé, former minister
a2058.name: Harouna Cissé
a2058.title: former minister
a2058.speech: “Alongside President ATT, Mangal was more powerful than ministers but despite all that, he remained himself.”

a2058.speaker: Hamadoun Touré, former minister and honorary president of Yiriwal Mopti
a2058.name: Hamadoun Touré
a2058.title: former minister and honorary president of Yiriwal Mopti
a2058.speech: “What impressed me most about Mangal is his efficiency at work, which is comparable to a Swiss watch, and his discretion, like that of a grave. He has virtues that are nowadays very rare in the administration in Africa.”

a2058.speaker: Ibrahim Diallo known as Number, first vice-president of Yirwal Mopti, and Nouhoum Tapily, president of the Ginna Dogon Association and former President of the Supreme Court
a2058.name: Ibrahim Diallo known as Number
a2058.title: first vice-president of Yirwal Mopti, and Nouhoum Tapily, president of the Ginna Dogon Association and former President of the Supreme Court
a2058.speech: All hailed and congratulated the happy recipient on this distinction.

a2058.speaker: A native of the Mopti region (anonymous)
a2058.name: A native of the Mopti region (anonymous)
a2058.speech: “Our pride comes above all from the fact that he received this medal not under ATT, whom he served for a long time, but rather under the current regime. That shows that it is his merit, his self-denial, that have been put to the fore.”

a2133.speaker: Arab Dheg Ahmed, commander of the US-trained Danab elite force in Jubaland (dismissed)
a2133.name: Arab Dheg Ahmed
a2133.title: commander of the US-trained Danab elite force in Jubaland (dismissed)
a2133.speech: Vehemently condemned authorities in Mogadishu for promoting military officers who had recently defected from Jubaland, asserting that Danab soldiers, who had long fought insurgents and made significant sacrifices, were unjustly overlooked, with their contributions dismissed and squandered.

a2133.speaker: Arab Dheg Ahmed, commander of the US-trained Danab elite force in Jubaland (dismissed)
a2133.name: Arab Dheg Ahmed
a2133.title: commander of the US-trained Danab elite force in Jubaland (dismissed)
a2133.speech: Raised alarm over the large-scale deployment of government troops to Raskamboni, some 250 kilometers south of Kismayo, warning that the troop buildup, aimed at ousting the Jubaland leader, would only provide an opportunity for the militant group Al-Shabaab to exploit the escalating tensions.

a2183.speaker: King Promise, Ghanaian Afrobeats artiste
a2183.name: King Promise
a2183.title: Ghanaian Afrobeats artiste
a2183.speech: In a brief speech, expressed gratitude to his fans and hinted that "he will be back," suggesting more wins could be on the horizon.

a2258.speaker: Professor Matthew Chersich, researcher at Wits RHI (Rural Health Institute)
a2258.name: Professor Matthew Chersich
a2258.title: researcher at Wits RHI (Rural Health Institute)
a2258.speech: Warned that there is a double burden on Africa as the continent is already being hit hardest by climate change but also has fewer resources to mount a sophisticated, wide-reaching, and sustained response: "The continent is already warming faster than other regions in the world but is also a low carbon emitter." ; "Right now we are in a phase of climate choice - the 10 years we have left to do something and stop making nature our slave or that choice will cascade so that we won't have a choice because nature will be at its tipping point."

a2258.speaker: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)
a2258.name: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)
a2258.speech: According to the IPCC, the northern and southern regions of the continent will become hotter and drier while the Sahel region will have increased rainfall.

a2258.speaker: Professor Matthew Chersich, researcher at Wits RHI
a2258.name: Professor Matthew Chersich
a2258.title: researcher at Wits RHI
a2258.speech: In his inaugural lecture, titled "how a medic came to study climate change", recounted how seven years ago he and his family were living in a small hamlet in Italy among a subsistence farming community, where increased extreme weather events quickly turned to lived reality and lived anxiety for the community that largely lived off the land ; "Climate change and public health already intersect in some key areas, which makes this field an important new area of research that we in public health must be turning our attention to. Some of the intersections with the public health response include how droughts and floods cause poverty and social disruption; there is also the response of emergency medicine in the case of increased extreme weather events that destroy infrastructure; then there's work looking at the effects on how climate change is shifting infectious disease patterns. All pathogens are temperature sensitive which means we'll see malaria spread to higher altitude areas; and then there's work on maternal health, which is an area where Wits University and I personally have a lot of background, so this became an obvious area that I wanted to focus on."

a2258.speaker: Professor Matthew Chersich, researcher at Wits RHI
a2258.name: Professor Matthew Chersich
a2258.title: researcher at Wits RHI
a2258.speech: Said choosing to focus on maternal health was strategic because maternal health has been the starting point for many past public health interventions including a massive reduction in mother-to-child transmission of HIV as well as interventions on nutrition and combating malaria ; said there was established foundational work done by Wits researchers in the late 1990s that measured the maternal-foetal temperature gradient: "The research found that a foetus is about half a degree warmer than its mother, which might not sound like much of a difference but if the mother's temperature rises with a fever to 40 degrees, the foetus is at 40.5 degrees and that makes an enormous difference physiologically."

a2258.speaker: Professor Matthew Chersich, researcher at Wits RHI
a2258.name: Professor Matthew Chersich
a2258.title: researcher at Wits RHI
a2258.speech: Said data from his research colleagues in Kenya is now showing that heat can be linked to preeclampsia, pre-term births, and complications in labour and childbirth - all of which can have knock-on effects for the mother and the child later on in life ; "What is happening physiologically to cause these pre-term impacts related to heat are changes to the endocrine system; oxidative or inflammatory changes; changes in placental perfusion, which can change the circulation of blood flow to the foetus that regulates heat; and there is increased exposure and risk to infections that include food, water, and vector-borne infections." ; said the evidence points to a looming crisis for maternal health and infant health and means "public health must be more than about treating disease".

a2258.speaker: Community health workers and women interviewed for Chersich and his colleagues' research
a2258.name: Community health workers and women interviewed for Chersich and his colleagues' research
a2258.speech: Gave revealing responses, including: "The foetus is not at peace when it is hot; it only finds peace when it is born" or "it is difficult to push in the heat" and "the baby has come before its time because it is too hot".

a2258.speaker: Professor Matthew Chersich, researcher at Wits RHI
a2258.name: Professor Matthew Chersich
a2258.title: researcher at Wits RHI
a2258.speech: Set out a multi-layered intervention strategy, a critical layer of which is using data science more effectively, including a five-year study that will span research teams across Africa and the United States: "It involves individual participant data and will be the largest data science project of its kind. Analysing this data will help us unlock some of the key questions and shape our interventions."

a2258.speaker: Professor Matthew Chersich, researcher at Wits RHI
a2258.name: Professor Matthew Chersich
a2258.title: researcher at Wits RHI
a2258.speech: Said there is a need for the public health sector to wake up to the necessity to enter more directly and deliberately into the climate change space, citing CHANCE (The Climate-Health Africa Network for Collaboration and Engagement), which he helped establish: "The health sector is ripe to intervene and this should include making submissions for funding from the Green Climate Fund to do the research and put in place the kinds of strategies that will help those who will be worst affected on the continent." ; "We in this sector understand the tricks and the tricksters. We know the playbook of big pharma, of the tobacco industry, the food manufacturing industry, the meat industry, and now also the fossil fuel industries." ; said public health also understands how to manage big global donors, citing long-standing PEPFAR and Global Fund projects on the continent, and that public health initiatives are where a groundswell for policy change can also take root.

a2258.speaker: Professor Matthew Chersich, researcher at Wits RHI
a2258.name: Professor Matthew Chersich
a2258.title: researcher at Wits RHI
a2258.speech: Said that even before policy, interventions need to start with awareness on the ground - healthcare workers knowing to make cool water available for pregnant women, especially during labour and childbirth; better advice on planning pregnancy according to seasonal temperatures; building more heat tolerant clinics and homes and planting more trees - all underpinned by a fight still for poverty reduction and building more equitable societies.

a2258.speaker: Professor Matthew Chersich, researcher at Wits RHI
a2258.name: Professor Matthew Chersich
a2258.title: researcher at Wits RHI
a2258.speech: Said behavioural change will come with personal discomfort and personal sacrifice - eating less meat, taking fewer flights, consuming more mindfully and accumulating less - and that for researchers and universities it is about questioning relationships with funders and companies and industries that advance the fossil fuel dependency agenda and pay not to fix problems but for a blind eye turned, green-washing, and silence ; "We have an abusive relationship with nature. It underlies our problems. We think we can eat and eat [from] nature and it will just replenish itself but there is no slowdown in emissions and we are on a trajectory of many places in the world being unliveable. All this means if we in public health want to fight disease then we need to also [be] part of systemic change. We need to stop the eating."

a2274.speaker: Government of Benin, Council of Ministers of Wednesday 11 September
a2274.name: Government of Benin
a2274.title: Council of Ministers of Wednesday 11 September
a2274.speech: Decided to commission a study for the definitive repair of the sand-arresting groyne at the port of Cotonou.

a2274.speaker: Independent international expert (report)
a2274.name: Independent international expert (report)
a2274.speech: It emerges from the expert's report that the primary cause of the infrastructure's defectiveness is negligence in its design, which led the consortium to carry out a provisional repair.

a2274.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB), Project Summary Note published in June 2023
a2274.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a2274.title: Project Summary Note published in June 2023
a2274.speech: According to the Project Summary Note published by the African Development Bank (June 2023), total financing for these projects amounts to 461.6 million euros, or 302.8 billion CFA francs, to be financed by various lenders as well as by the equity of the Autonomous Port of Cotonou.

a2274.speaker: Council of Ministers of 11 November 2020
a2274.name: Council of Ministers of 11 November 2020
a2274.speech: Gave its agreement for contracting with the architectural firm Koffi & Diabaté for the project management mission of the Maritime Business Centre project.

a2344.speaker: Guillaume Aguettant, country director of Care Bénin/Togo
a2344.name: Guillaume Aguettant
a2344.title: country director of Care Bénin/Togo
a2344.speech: Says that since the signing of the headquarters agreement on 9 September 1999 in Benin, Care has played a crucial role in improving communities' living conditions and building the capacity of local partners ; welcomes that in twenty-five years of existence Care Bénin has established itself as a key development actor, operating in all 77 communes of the country with a strong concentration in the four northern departments ; indicates that in 2023 the organisation reached nearly 500,000 people through 21 development projects and two humanitarian projects, with a total budget of 14.37 million dollars, or 8.69 billion CFA francs.

a2344.speaker: Participants in Care programmes and projects, implementing partners and former staff (testimonies gathered in a documentary film and during the webinar)
a2344.name: Participants in Care programmes and projects
a2344.title: implementing partners and former staff (testimonies gathered in a documentary film and during the webinar)
a2344.speech: Their testimonies are laudatory, saying Care Bénin has helped to "change the life" of many, through the fight against gender-based violence, increased leadership of girls and women, conflict prevention and disaster preparedness, governance and social accountability, food and nutrition and sexual and reproductive health.

a2344.speaker: Claudine Awuté Mensah, vice-president for Programmes and Operations at Care International and former country director of Care Bénin/Togo
a2344.name: Claudine Awuté Mensah
a2344.title: vice-president for Programmes and Operations at Care International and former country director of Care Bénin/Togo
a2344.speech: Praises that the organisation stands out for its dynamic and committed staff, with a strong representation of young people under 35, and constitutes a family in which talents emerge and flourish in the service of communities.

a2344.speaker: Balla Sidibé, Care's regional director for West Africa
a2344.name: Balla Sidibé
a2344.title: Care's regional director for West Africa
a2344.speech: Stresses that Care has been able to build a solid and diversified network of partners, including international institutions such as USAID, the World Bank, the European Union, the Kingdom of the Netherlands and Swiss Cooperation, as well as members of Care International such as Care USA, Care France, Care Luxembourg and Care Canada ; indicates that this diversity of partnerships enables the organisation to run multisectoral projects meeting the needs of the most vulnerable populations.

a2344.speaker: Alain Troukou, director of Programme Quality and Resource Mobilisation at Care Bénin
a2344.name: Alain Troukou
a2344.title: director of Programme Quality and Resource Mobilisation at Care Bénin
a2344.speech: Assures that Care Bénin reaffirms its commitment to continuing its work in four priority areas: economic justice and gender, maternal, child and youth health, food and nutrition security, and emergency preparedness and response ; continues that with the ambition of reaching 2.8 million people by 2026, the organisation looks to the future with the will to contribute to defeating poverty and social injustice.

a2440.speaker: USAID (statement)
a2440.name: USAID (statement)
a2440.speech: “This assistance, which will be implemented by consortiums led by USAID partners Catholic Relief Services and Cultivating New Frontiers in Agriculture, will support marginalized households to build sustainable livelihoods, develop financial capital and increase their savings and assets,” USAID said in a statement.

a2440.speaker: United States government
a2440.name: United States government
a2440.speech: Announced an allocation of over $22 million in additional aid to boost resilience and food security for the most vulnerable populations in Madagascar, marking the initiation of two new five-year projects in the Androy, Anosy and Atsimo Atsinanana regions benefiting about 88,000 extremely impoverished and marginalised households.

a2482.speaker: Brandon Hudspeth, United States representative (Charge d'Affaires) in Namibia
a2482.name: Brandon Hudspeth
a2482.title: United States representative (Charge d'Affaires) in Namibia
a2482.speech: Highlighted US support to Namibia through PEPFAR.

a2482.speaker: Dorothy Kabula, Governor of the Zambezi Region
a2482.name: Dorothy Kabula
a2482.title: Governor of the Zambezi Region
a2482.speech: Praised the United States for its great support: "It is a good thing. We are doing well in our health services in Namibia. The US has been a friend of Namibia for a long time. We are doing well on the health side in Namibia. Keep on doing so. Do not stop those medicines. The friendship with Namibia should continue."

a2482.speaker: Brandon Hudspeth, United States representative (Charge d'Affaires) in Namibia
a2482.name: Brandon Hudspeth
a2482.title: United States representative (Charge d'Affaires) in Namibia
a2482.speech: Emphasised the spirit of partnership behind the successes achieved in Namibia: "I want to emphasise the issue of partnership because, yes, the US has provided support and technical advice, but it is the partnership with Namibians, with the health ministry, that has made these programmes succeed. We have had PEPFAR services in other countries, but they do not look the way they look in Namibia... it is because of you."

a2482.speaker: Brandon Hudspeth, United States representative (Charge d'Affaires) in Namibia
a2482.name: Brandon Hudspeth
a2482.title: United States representative (Charge d'Affaires) in Namibia
a2482.speech: Reflecting on the visit, added: "It has been a good visit, especially because of the partnership with the health ministry. What was most encouraging was meeting patients and seeing how they have embraced this and the benefit of passing it on to coming generations. That is the foundation of everything."

a2482.speaker: Taimi Amaambo, Deputy Executive Director of the Ministry of Health and Social Services
a2482.name: Taimi Amaambo
a2482.title: Deputy Executive Director of the Ministry of Health and Social Services
a2482.speech: Spoke about the importance of partnership in planning between Namibia and the US government: "What makes this partnership distinctive is that all our plans are joint, we organise activities together. It is not that the US government says 'this is what you must do.' Rather, they are needs that we identify together. That is why we can see people who are now counsellors, who live with HIV, helping others who are in the same situation." She added that the partnership goes beyond health facilities.

a2552.speaker: Solomon Kebede, press and information officer (European Union)
a2552.name: Solomon Kebede
a2552.title: press and information officer (European Union)
a2552.speech: Said the EU has been working with the Productive Safety Net Program since its launch in 2005.

a2701.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a2701.name: Abdoulaye Diop
a2701.title: Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a2701.speech: Told Sputnik that the countries of the Sahel Alliance are counting on Russia's help to create a military industry: "We are already working with Russia on several projects, whether in the security field, in the field of diplomacy or on the economic level; our countries wish to strengthen our capacities and develop autonomy, so that we can move out of patterns of dependence." ; Stressed that the acquisition of military equipment is becoming an increasingly important need; the AES countries will try "to ensure that, with the Russian partner, which has technology and proven experience, in conjunction with Russian companies and the Russian state, we can also create military capacities within the AES area," which will reduce their "dependence on imports of military equipment" and create new jobs.

a2748.speaker: Embassy of the United States in Côte d'Ivoire (press release)
a2748.name: Embassy of the United States in Côte d'Ivoire (press release)
a2748.speech: Announced the recent award of six grants for a total amount of 75,000 dollars (more than 45 million CFA francs) under the Ambassador's Self-Help Assistance Programme and the Julia Taft Fund for Refugees: “Funded by the American people, these grants will support community efforts aimed at improving access to drinking water, processing agricultural products, empowering vulnerable groups — including women, young people and people with disabilities — as well as improving health and nutrition.” The release specified that the beneficiary organisations represent rural communities across Côte d'Ivoire, that five grants are awarded under the Ambassador's Self-Help Assistance Programme and the sixth comes from the Julia Taft Fund for Refugees, and that 50 families in the Dimbokro region will see their incomes rise by 40%; it described the Action de Vie “project [that] aims to contribute to reducing unemployment among young people and women by creating job opportunities in several sectors, including agro-industry value chains and artisanal mining” with “550 women and young people targeted in the Man region” and “1,150 people living in the three districts” as indirect beneficiaries, and the Soubré fish-pond project that “will directly benefit some fifty women for the production of tilapia, and indirectly 100 other families.”

a2888.speaker: James Knight, US Ambassador to Benin
a2888.name: James Knight
a2888.title: US Ambassador to Benin
a2888.speech: In the speech he delivered at the reception, Ambassador Knight said: "Tonight's event represents for me a sign of encouragement and an exhortation to greater political commitment for the happiness of the Beninese people."

a2888.speaker: Embassy of the United States of America (press release)
a2888.name: Embassy of the United States of America (press release)
a2888.speech: USAID celebrated on 27 and 28 October 2011 in Abomey the 50th anniversary of its creation and the 20th anniversary of its establishment in Benin ; stated that since the beginning of its engagement in Benin, USAID has invested a total of $124 million in the health sector, 110,235,265 US dollars in the education sector, and more than $12,000,000 in social services, and set out the results of the Integrated Family Health Project (PISAF) and the EMPOWER project.

a2942.speaker: Siboniso Masilela, Under Secretary / acting Principal Secretary, Ministry of Economic Planning and Development (representing Principal Secretary Thabsile Mlangeni)
a2942.name: Siboniso Masilela
a2942.title: Under Secretary / acting Principal Secretary, Ministry of Economic Planning and Development (representing Principal Secretary Thabsile Mlangeni)
a2942.speech: Warmly opened and blessed the workshop, extending his sincere welcome and thanking the attendees for their commitment to the process, underscoring the collective importance of the initiative.

a2942.speaker: Workshop participants / key stakeholders
a2942.name: Workshop participants / key stakeholders
a2942.speech: Actively shared their insights and provided essential feedback, repeatedly highlighting the importance of creating a policy that not only sets clear expectations but also genuinely empowers all ministries to collaborate effectively; expressed their deep gratitude for the opportunity to contribute meaningfully to such a significant national initiative.

a2942.speaker: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Eswatini country programme document (2016-2020)
a2942.name: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Eswatini country programme document (2016-2020)
a2942.speech: Identified priorities for UNDP's interventions that were highly relevant to the country's development challenges, established around objectives in line with the National Development Strategy 2013-2022, the King's Vision 2022 and the United Nations Development Assistance Framework outcomes, with Eswatini planned to contribute to inclusive economic growth and sustainable development, and resilience and risk reduction incorporating sustainable natural resource management and good governance, equity and citizen participation; noted that activities implemented by UNDP have too often deviated from its set objectives and planned outputs, and that new projects and activities offer opportunities to diversify and attract new funding in areas such as youth, innovation and energy efficiency, but also increase the risk of moving away from UNDP's programme objectives.

a3217.speaker: Standard Bank Plc
a3217.name: Standard Bank Plc
a3217.speech: Says it looks forward to partnering government and other key stakeholders to support new President Arthur Peter Mutharika’s plan to immediately tackle prevailing macro-economic challenges.

a3217.speaker: Phillip Madinga, Standard Bank Chief Executive and Bankers Association of Malawi (BAM) president
a3217.name: Phillip Madinga
a3217.title: Standard Bank Chief Executive and Bankers Association of Malawi (BAM) president
a3217.speech: In an interview on the sidelines of the inauguration ceremony at Kamuzu Stadium, welcomed the new administration’s resolve for a return to economic stability, predictability and strong governance ; “Attracting FDI from key economies such as the US and China, as outlined in his Excellency the President Prof. Arthur Peter Mutharika’s inauguration speech, is also critical in unlocking Malawi’ growth potential and delivering meaningful economic recovery” ; “We also note the President’s determination to seek a renewal of relations with the US through his special friendship with the US President Donald Trump. Easing diplomatic hurdles with the US should set the stage for dialogue aimed at finding solutions for Malawi’s economy, trade and diplomatic relations” ; “The loss of development and technical support following USAID’s departure would require dialogue aimed at exploring solutions for the country.”

a3217.speaker: Phillip Madinga, Standard Bank Chief Executive
a3217.name: Phillip Madinga
a3217.title: Standard Bank Chief Executive
a3217.speech: Added that they look forward to a strong private and public partnership in the next critical three months of the government’s transition process, saying: “The stage should be prepared for a re-set of a new economic trajectory where Malawi’s resolve to return to stability through fiscal discipline and governance, dialogue with bilateral and multilateral donors and creditors and improved trade relations, is unambiguous.”

a3217.speaker: Arthur Peter Mutharika, President of Malawi (inaugural speech)
a3217.name: Arthur Peter Mutharika
a3217.title: President of Malawi (inaugural speech)
a3217.speech: “Wisdom tells us that in order to solve a problem, you must know the problem. We must begin by accepting our situation as it is. Our immediate problem is that we have inherited a country in a crisis — Malawi is in the middle of an economic crisis. There is no food in the country and the cost of maize is very high. Malawians cannot afford the cost of living; there is no forex, businesses are failing and collapsing every day; we have acute fuel shortages because there is no forex. The cost of fuel is unnecessarily high because of corruption and a badly flawed procurement system. There is no money in government. Borrowing is extremely high — and nobody knows where the borrowed money has gone. But there is good news though — Malawi’s crisis is a man-made crisis. Our situation is not a natural tragedy beyond human capacity; our situation is not a permanent condition. Any problem created by humans can be solved by humans. Malawi’s situation is a problem we can solve, and solve it we will. We will fix this country.” ; “But, fixing this country will not be easy — this must be clear. Rebuilding this country will not be easy. It is easy to destroy what others have built, but difficult to rebuild what others have destroyed. It will be tough. And we must be tougher. I don’t promise you milk and honey. I promise you hard work, tough and painful decisions. The only way to rebuilding this country is to make tough decisions. Above all, I ask for your patience. In the end, we will all be happy that we have a country that nourishes our dreams and the aspirations of our children. With patience, discipline and hard work, we will make Malawi a country where we are happy to live in.”

a3217.speaker: Arthur Peter Mutharika, President of Malawi (inaugural speech)
a3217.name: Arthur Peter Mutharika
a3217.title: President of Malawi (inaugural speech)
a3217.speech: “There is another good news. The DPP Government is ready to govern and ready to rebuild this country. We have a clear, comprehensive development and governance blueprint articulating a new vision and a new agenda for transforming Malawi. Our manifesto is a pledge for total transformation!” ; “I promised that we would be back — and today, we are back with a new vision, a new DPP agenda. We are back by the will of God, and the collective will of the people. And in different ways, we have all seen the invisible hand of God in this historic election — this, we should never forget!” ; “Remember, this election has told us that Malawians are united in one vision, dream, as one country, with one purpose. Let us come to serve the will of the people. We all wanted change. We voted for change. We expect change. I promise you real change. Zinthu zisintha! But real change must begin with us, each one of us. If you want a different Malawi, if you want different results, then let us begin to think differently, and do things differently.”

a3217.speaker: Arthur Peter Mutharika, President of Malawi (inaugural speech)
a3217.name: Arthur Peter Mutharika
a3217.title: President of Malawi (inaugural speech)
a3217.speech: On corruption and governance: “To all my friends in the DPP and anyone in any public office, remember this! Malawi belongs to its people. This country does not belong to any person, any tribe or any political party. Malawi does not belong to the DPP either. Malawi belongs to us all. Let us be in government to serve the people; not to serve our bellies, not to serve our families. Tisiye kuganiza kuti tikulowa m’boma kuti tidyelele. This is the attitude that is killing this country. It’s not about kudyelela. Government is not a feast. Being in Government is about serving to deliver, to change our economic situation, to create jobs, and to help everyone prosper in their businesses, farming and education. It is that feasting spirit; it is that tidyelele spirit which makes people go wild into corruption, theft, looting and destroying this country. Stop destroying this country! The honeymoon of looting government is over! You are dealing with a different President now. And you are looking at a different President. I will not allow anyone to destroy this country under my watch, and I mean anyone! The Vice-President and I want to see discipline and sanity everywhere in government. We will clean up the house to restore discipline and integrity in government as we challenge every Malawian to change our mindset. The Vice-President and I will not allow you to bring back chaos while we clean up the house. Never say, I never warned you! So, let us come to serve the many people who voted for us. We voted as one people, and let us rise above our differences to change this country as one people.”

a3217.speaker: Arthur Peter Mutharika, President of Malawi (inaugural speech)
a3217.name: Arthur Peter Mutharika
a3217.title: President of Malawi (inaugural speech)
a3217.speech: While applauding Malawians for their vote, extended his vote of thanks to the Catholic Bishops, the Muslim leadership and all Christians and other faiths “for standing up against evil, corruption and state sponsored terror” ; “Malawians voted out corruption, blatant theft, heartless looting, state terrorism and wanton destruction. The spirit that destroys our nation does not come from outside our borders — it comes from amongst us, from within us. We are the people destroying our own country. There is a disease of the spirit that we suffer as a country. And I ask all you leaders of faith to help us heal this nation.”

a3217.speaker: Arthur Peter Mutharika, President of Malawi (inaugural speech)
a3217.name: Arthur Peter Mutharika
a3217.title: President of Malawi (inaugural speech)
a3217.speech: Extended the vote of thanks to development partners who wished Malawi well from different capitals across the world — calling on the Dean of the Diplomatic Corps to convey the message to the diplomatic community for supporting Malawians to conduct a peaceful and credible election: “You helped Malawians to vote for their will. Our special thanks particularly go to SADC and the UNDP for your efforts and support in the past election. Malawi cannot survive outside the international community. But I have one request to all our friends in the international community, please send us investors and every support you can. Malawi is now open for business. Those of you who doubted if Malawi can be trusted with your hard-earned financial support from your tax payers, let me say, yes! You can trust my government on financial management. Give us support, and we will deliver to the people. My previous government is proof of that fact. In a particular way, I want to thank the US Government and the UK Government, together with the entire European Community for standing up against corruption, theft of public resources, and reckless looting of the national treasury. You quietly spoke in diplomatic whispers, but Malawians heard your goodwill in their villages and public markets where we suffered the high cost of living. To President Donald Trump, your message of congratulations and goodwill found us well. We will soon be sending you a delegation to negotiate the Malawi situation. There are critical areas we must address especially after the exit of USAID and the many programs they supported. I am sure we can strike a deal of some kind. To our neighbours and friends in Zambia, Tanzania, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, Botswana, South Africa, and the entire SADC Region, up to Kenya and beyond, I look forward to working with you again in the spirit of harmony and goodwill for our people.”

a3288.speaker: Ali Yusuf Ali Hosh, Minister of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation of Somalia, and George Conway, Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General/Resident Coordinator/Humanitarian Coordinator
a3288.name: Ali Yusuf Ali Hosh
a3288.title: Minister of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation of Somalia, and George Conway, Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General/Resident Coordinator/Humanitarian Coordinator
a3288.speech: Discussed key national priorities including reconciliation, humanitarian assistance and strengthening the bilateral cooperation between the two sides.

a3443.speaker: Zul Kifl Salami, Special Envoy (chargé de mission) of the Head of State of Benin
a3443.name: Zul Kifl Salami
a3443.title: Special Envoy (chargé de mission) of the Head of State of Benin
a3443.speech: At a press conference in Cotonou on Friday 8 November, gave details of the financing agreements and their impact on the country's development: "The Beninese delegation really attended every appointment and in the end we signed four major financing agreements. It got itself out of trouble, if I may say so, during the assembly, with a jackpot of 74.5 billion francs. And the amount alone is not enough. These are essentially concessional financings, that is to say with a maturity that can go up to 30 years, with interest rates of around 1.75 or 2%. All of which is precisely compatible with the financing of infrastructure in a developing country."

a3443.speaker: Zul Kifl Salami, Special Envoy of the Head of State of Benin
a3443.name: Zul Kifl Salami
a3443.title: Special Envoy of the Head of State of Benin
a3443.speech: Said Benin's ambition under the National Development Plan (PND) 2018-2025 is to be realised with the support of partners; considered that the credibility Benin enjoys on the financial market is reassuring to partners, awarding a vote of satisfaction to the leadership and vision of the President of the Republic.

a3443.speaker: Zul Kifl Salami, Special Envoy of the Head of State of Benin
a3443.name: Zul Kifl Salami
a3443.title: Special Envoy of the Head of State of Benin
a3443.speech: Said the Annual Meetings of the IMF and the World Bank were historic, marking the 80th anniversary of the Bretton Woods conference, the accession of Liechtenstein as the IMF's 191st member country, and the historic decision to grant an additional seat to sub-Saharan Africa: "It will have more of a say. It will bring its know-how. It will also bring its economic weight, because sub-Saharan Africa means mineral resources, oil resources, agriculture and the like, all of which will allow better visibility for sub-Saharan Africa and better credibility and respectability for our countries. This calls for a duty on our part, which is that we capitalise on this decision, this additional seat, to really make our contribution to the Fund's deliberations and ultimately solve the problems that sub-Saharan African countries most face."

a3443.speaker: Zul Kifl Salami, Special Envoy of the Head of State of Benin
a3443.name: Zul Kifl Salami
a3443.title: Special Envoy of the Head of State of Benin
a3443.speech: Appreciating the contribution of the Beninese delegation led by Minister of State Romuald Wadagni, he called for more commitment and responsibility: "These fantastic results that we have achieved with the signing of the four agreements call for a duty on our part, which is that we show more agility and speed in conducting projects, because it is not enough to have resources; the human resources must also be able to steer these projects so that the impact the people expect, in terms of poverty alleviation and shared prosperity, can be achieved as quickly as possible."

a3562.speaker: Bank of Industry (BoI) (statement)
a3562.name: Bank of Industry (BoI) (statement)
a3562.speech: Stated that it secured €1.425 billion from the senior phase of its global loan syndication scheme, said the loan is the largest in its history and represents a 42.5 percent oversubscription from international financial markets, and that the facility includes a fully and partially guaranteed tranche by the Africa Finance Corporation (AFC): “Previously, Bank of Industry had raised EUR 1,000,000,000 via a Term Loan syndicated facility In July 2022, which has been successfully repaid in July 2024” ; “The performance of the syndication is a mark of confidence in the bank and indeed in the Nigerian economy by foreign investors who perceive a bright future for the country.”

a3562.speaker: Bank of Industry (BoI) (statement)
a3562.name: Bank of Industry (BoI) (statement)
a3562.speech: Noted that the proceeds of the loan would help to finance a growing demand for its funds across the country; said it appointed the AFC and Standard Chartered Bank as global coordinators for the €1 billion syndicated term loan facility: “Africa Finance Corporation, African Export-Import Bank, First Abu Dhabi Bank PJSC, FirstRand Bank Limited (London Branch), acting through its Rand Merchant Bank division, Mashreqbank psc, SMBC Bank International plc, and Standard Chartered Bank were appointed as the initial mandated lead arrangers and bookrunners” ; “Absa Bank Limited (acting through its corporate and investment banking division) and its affiliates and Export-Import Bank of India London Branch have also joined the facility as initial mandated lead arrangers” ; said it is looking forward to a successful conclusion of the ongoing general phase, given the level of interest expressed by local and international banks and investors.

a3562.speaker: Olasupo Olusi, managing director and chief executive officer of the Bank of Industry
a3562.name: Olasupo Olusi
a3562.title: managing director and chief executive officer of the Bank of Industry
a3562.speech: Attributed the achievement to the hard work and dedication of the institution’s management: “This the largest syndication in the Bank’s history and is testament to the hard work and dedication of the management of BoI to ensuring that much needed low interest and longer tenured funds are available to Nigeria’s growing private sector in line with the vision of his excellency President Bola Ahmed Tinubu” ; “We are grateful for the support received from the CBN and other agencies of government” ; assured that the bank, under his leadership, would continue to work with global development financial institutions to ensure better loan terms for Nigeria’s private enterprises.

a3563.speaker: Julia Vityazeva (social-media post)
a3563.name: Julia Vityazeva (social-media post)
a3563.speech: “#For GAGA. The United States voted against the resolution on UN cooperation with the Council of Europe, as it was ‘condemning Russian aggression in Ukraine,’ and this does not help achieve peace. The decision of the United States was supported by Belarus, Russia, Eritrea. This is the second time Washington has voted against a resolution condemning Moscow.”

a3587.speaker: Emirates Airlines (statement)
a3587.name: Emirates Airlines (statement)
a3587.speech: A statement by Emirates confirmed that its passengers experienced minimal disruptions to their travel plans after Monday's regional events; the statement said that the airline had quickly activated its "robust contingency and disruption plans, with no diversions, only a small number of cancellations and a few flights experiencing longer flight paths due to airspace congestion. Despite rapidly evolving regional developments, it's been business as usual across the Emirates network. In the past two weeks, Emirates has maintained scheduled services by rerouting flights to avoid conflict zones, successfully serving over 1.7 million passengers on more than 5,800 flights across its global network and delivering certainty to their travel plans when they needed it the most, while upholding its commitment to safe, reliable travel."

a3587.speaker: Emirates Airlines
a3587.name: Emirates Airlines
a3587.speech: said it took immediate action by suspending flights only to areas directly impacted by conflict while maintaining operations to all other destinations; said services to Amman and Beirut were briefly suspended but resumed quickly, demonstrating Emirates' ability to nimbly adapt its operations while prioritising safety, and helping thousands of families start their summer holidays.

a3587.speaker: Emirates Airlines
a3587.name: Emirates Airlines
a3587.speech: restated that the safety of its passengers and crew was its absolute priority, assuring that it would never fly if it was not safe to do so, and emphasises that it continuously monitors developments, coordinates with aviation authorities, and assesses every potential risk to ensure all flights are safely rerouted away from conflict zones, all the while meeting the most stringent regulatory requirements.

a3587.speaker: Emirates Airlines (circular on its website)
a3587.name: Emirates Airlines (circular on its website)
a3587.speech: A circular obtained on the airline's website indicated that the rerouting was due to the "recent regional situation" in Asia and its close regions; the airline said that it would not divert its scheduled operations, but warned that there might be flight delays.

a3597.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a3597.name: Joe Biden
a3597.title: US President
a3597.speech: Confirming the agreement, said in a statement that the deal would “halt the fighting in Gaza, surge much needed-humanitarian assistance to Palestinian civilians, and reunite the hostages with their families after more than 15 months in captivity.”

a3597.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect (post on Truth Social)
a3597.name: Donald Trump
a3597.title: US President-elect (post on Truth Social)
a3597.speech: stated that a hostage deal had been reached and hostages held by Hamas would be “released shortly.” “We have a deal for the hostage in the Middle East. They will be released shortly,” Mr Trump posted on Truth Social, his social media platform.

a3597.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a3597.name: Donald Trump
a3597.title: US President-elect
a3597.speech: warned that there would be “hell to pay” if Hamas failed to release Israeli hostages before he takes office.

a3597.speaker: CNN
a3597.name: CNN
a3597.speech: According to CNN, implementation is likely to start on Sunday with the release of hostages on both sides.

a3597.speaker: Antony Blinken, US Secretary of State
a3597.name: Antony Blinken
a3597.title: US Secretary of State
a3597.speech: stated that the proposed deal was built on a framework introduced by the Biden administration in May.

a3597.speaker: Gaza Civil Defense
a3597.name: Gaza Civil Defense
a3597.speech: has urged residents to avoid celebratory gunfire as the region anticipates the finalisation of the ceasefire agreement. The agency warned that such actions could lead to injuries. “We call upon you to refrain from firing bullets in the air for fear of injuring the displaced people in the tents and shelters,” it said. “We do not want to be saddened by more martyrs and wounded.”

a3740.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a3740.name: Daniel Chapo
a3740.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a3740.speech: Invites Algerian businesspeople to get a close look at the business opportunities existing in Mozambique by investing in concrete projects, assuring them that “the Mozambican government is available to support and facilitate the steps necessary for partnerships to become a reality” ; explained that Mozambique and Algeria are sister countries that achieved independence with mutual support and that now it is time to follow the same example for economic independence, thereby improving the living conditions of their peoples ; stressed that the country has numerous business opportunities in hydrocarbons and energy, the pharmaceutical industry and health, tourism and aviation, and education and training.

a3740.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a3740.name: Daniel Chapo
a3740.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a3740.speech: On hydrocarbons: revealed that “Mozambique is becoming one of the great producers of natural gas in Africa and in the world,” seeking partnerships in natural gas refining, petrochemicals and the use of gas for industrialisation ; “We currently have five projects, one in which we have already been exporting gas for more than 20 years, in the south of the country, in Temane, Inhambane province, which is being exploited by the South African company Sasol” ; “But at this moment we are working on four projects in the northern zone of the country, which are one of the largest gas discoveries in the world. We have four projects there. One by the Italian company ENI, and we are exploring gas in a project of about seven billion dollars” ; underlined that investments under way total a cumulative of close to 50 billion dollars, resulting in “many business opportunities” ; praised the memorandum between the National Hydrocarbons Company (ENH) and the Algerian oil company SONATRACH as “an important basis for strengthening staff training, technology transfer and the establishment of joint ventures between Algerian and Mozambican companies in the hydrocarbons sector.”

a3740.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a3740.name: Daniel Chapo
a3740.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a3740.speech: On the pharmaceutical industry and health: showed interest in strengthening Mozambique's pharmaceutical industry, looking to Algeria “as the only reference example in Africa”; added that Mozambique is looking for local producers of medicines, including vaccines, and medical equipment, since it currently depends on imports for almost 100%, above all from India, and that it also prioritises clinics and hospitals, even private ones, to be supported by Algeria's private sector.

a3740.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a3740.name: Daniel Chapo
a3740.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a3740.speech: On tourism and transport: highlighted the country's 2,700 km coastline, paradisiacal beaches and islands, nature reserves and “an enviable historical and cultural heritage”; announced that in November an international tourism conference will be held in Inhambane, Vilankulo, but that investment is still lacking; stressed that an air link between Maputo and Algiers through Air Algérie “would be a great catalyst for tourism and business between the two countries”; emphasised opportunities in the development and logistics corridors, where “Mozambique controls the three largest corridors of southern Africa: the ports of Maputo, Beira and Nacala,” which “give direct access to seven landlocked interior countries that depend on Mozambique.”

a3740.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a3740.name: Daniel Chapo
a3740.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a3740.speech: On education and agriculture: stressed that “cooperation in education and study grants has been exemplary between the two countries,” showing interest in deepening the partnership, above all in hydrocarbons, engineering and health; stressed that “Mozambique has a great expanse of arable land and water” and could “produce large quantities of fruit” ; “Mozambique has the agro-ecological conditions to produce cashew nuts... In fact, Mozambique was once the world's largest producer of cashew nuts and we can once again put cashew production into industrial quantities (...) and we can also produce other agricultural products for Algeria, but also to export to the world.”

a3740.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a3740.name: Daniel Chapo
a3740.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a3740.speech: Said Mozambique is ready to offer partnerships and work with Algerian businesspeople to create jobs for the youth of both countries and accelerate the industrialisation of both; ended by stressing the need for both countries to continue developing each other mutually, “otherwise the resources will develop Europe, Asia, China and other countries,” which are also brothers “but Africa first, and if we do not find a solution we will turn to our other brothers [non-Africans]; this is our philosophy.”

a3865.speaker: Mary Sapeza, 21, mother from Kwatani Village, Phalombe
a3865.name: Mary Sapeza
a3865.title: 21, mother from Kwatani Village, Phalombe
a3865.speech: “I only harvested two bags of maize last growing season and that lasted until May,” she says with exhaustion. “Now I do piecework to get daily food.” ; “Now weight has improved to 7.5 kilogrammes,” says Sapeza, proudly clutching her baby’s health passport.

a3865.speaker: Beatrice Muchiri, 25, mother from Mwambeni Village, Phalombe
a3865.name: Beatrice Muchiri
a3865.title: 25, mother from Mwambeni Village, Phalombe
a3865.speech: Says her 19-month-old daughter is also recovering from wasting fuelled by drought: “I have been coming here weekly, and she is getting better. Her appetite is back.”

a3865.speaker: Lucy Ndiwo, Phalombe chief nutrition, HIV and Aids officer
a3865.name: Lucy Ndiwo
a3865.title: Phalombe chief nutrition, HIV and Aids officer
a3865.speech: “Our district experiences disasters which disrupt food production almost every year. This leaves families unable to feed themselves and malnutrition cases keep rising, especially among children and pregnant women.”

a3865.speaker: 2024 Malawi Demographic and Health Survey
a3865.name: 2024 Malawi Demographic and Health Survey
a3865.speech: According to the survey, 38.7 percent of children under five are stunted, 10 percent are underweight and two percent are wasted.

a3865.speaker: Health workers
a3865.name: Health workers
a3865.speech: Say poor nutrition in the critical first 1 000 days of life causes irreversible damage to a child’s health, physical growth, learning and productivity.

a3865.speaker: Rebecca Adda-Dontoh, United Nations resident coordinator in Malawi
a3865.name: Rebecca Adda-Dontoh
a3865.title: United Nations resident coordinator in Malawi
a3865.speech: Said the UN is committed to support Malawi’s health and nutrition agenda: “Malawi 2063 prioritises a healthy population as a cornerstone for national development. The SDGs echo the same. So, malnutrition is not just a health issue—it is a development bottleneck.” ; “We are not going anywhere. The UN will continue standing with Malawi, its people and its systems, to build resilience and secure a better future.”

a4187.speaker: Vladimir Putin, President of Russia
a4187.name: Vladimir Putin
a4187.title: President of Russia
a4187.speech: said on Wednesday up to 30 nations have expressed interest in joining the bloc, which now counts nine members after Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) joined earlier this year.

a4187.speaker: European Union
a4187.name: European Union
a4187.speech: on Wednesday called for Brics to use the opportunity to urge Putin to “immediately end the war on the Ukrainian people”.

a4187.speaker: Sources (anonymous)
a4187.name: Sources (anonymous)
a4187.speech: said every approach on the subject [of the conflict in Ukraine, raised by Ramaphosa, Modi and Xi ahead of the leaders' session] was met with silence.

a4187.speaker: Narendra Modi, Indian Prime Minister
a4187.name: Narendra Modi
a4187.title: Indian Prime Minister
a4187.speech: told reporters: “We have been in constant touch over the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. We believe that disputes should only be resolved peacefully. We totally support efforts to quickly restore peace and stability.”

a4187.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a4187.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4187.title: President of South Africa
a4187.speech: In published remarks, gave reassurances that South Africa's historic friendship with Russia remained intact: “We continue to see Russia as a valued ally, as a valued friend, who supported us right from the beginning: from the days of our struggle against apartheid, right through to now.”

a4187.speaker: South African presidency
a4187.name: South African presidency
